title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Protocol Introduction (Rev. 37, Issued: 10-17-08; Effective/Implementation Date: 10-17-08)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospitals are required to be in compliance with the Federal requirements set forth in the Medicare Conditions of Participation (CoP) in order to receive Medicare/Medicaid payment. The goal of a hospital survey is to determine if the hospital is in compliance with the CoP set forth at 42 CFR Part 482. Also, where appropriate, the hospital must be in compliance with the PPS exclusionary criteria at 42 CFR 412.20 Subpart B and the swing-bed requirements at 42 CFR 482.66

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Certification of hospital compliance with the CoP is accomplished through observations, interviews, and document/record reviews. The survey process focuses on a hospital's performance of patient-focused and organizational functions and processes. The hospital survey is the means used to assess compliance with Federal health, safety, and quality standards that will assure that the beneficiary receives safe, quality care and services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Regulatory and Policy Reference

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The Medicare Conditions of Participation for hospitals are found at 42CFR Part 482.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Survey authority and compliance regulations can be found at 42 CFR Part 488 Subpart A.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Should an individual or entity (hospital) refuse to allow immediate access upon reasonable request to either a State Agency or CMS surveyor, the Office of the Inspector General (OIG) may exclude the hospital from participation in all Federal healthcare programs in accordance with 42 CFR 1001.1301.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The regulatory authority for the photocopying of records and information during the survey is found at 42 CFR 489.53(a)(13).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The CMS State Operations Manual (SOM) provides CMS policy regarding survey and certification activities.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Surveyors assess the hospital's compliance with the CoP for all services, areas and locations in which the provider receives reimbursement for patient care services billed under its provider number.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Although the survey generally occurs during daytime working hours (Monday through Friday), surveyors may conduct the survey at other times. This may include weekends and times outside of normal daytime (Monday through Friday) working hours. When the survey begins at times outside of normal work times, the survey team modifies the survey, if needed, in recognition of patients' activities and the staff available.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: All hospital surveys are unannounced. Do not provide hospitals with advance notice of the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Modules for Specialized Hospital Services

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The modules for PPS-exempt units (psychiatric and rehabilitation), psychiatric hospitals, rehabilitation hospitals and swing-bed hospitals are attached to this document. The survey team is expected to use all the modules that apply to the hospital being surveyed. For example, if the hospital has swing-beds, a PPS excluded rehabilitation unit, and a PPS excluded psychiatric unit, the team will use those three modules in addition to this protocol to conduct the survey. If the hospital is a rehabilitation hospital, the team will use the rehabilitation hospital module in addition to this protocol to conduct the survey. If the hospital is a psychiatric hospital and if the survey team will be assessing the hospital's compliance with both the hospital CoPs and psychiatric hospital special conditions, the team will use the psychiatric hospital module in addition to this protocol to conduct the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Team

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Size and Composition

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The SA (or the RO for Federal teams) decides the composition and size of the team. In general, a suggested survey team for a full survey of a mid-size hospital would include two- four surveyors who will be at the facility for 3 or more days. Each hospital survey team should include at least one RN with hospital survey experience, as well as other surveyors who have the expertise needed to determine whether the facility is in compliance. Survey team size and composition are normally based on the following factors:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Size of the facility to be surveyed, based on average daily census;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Complexity of services offered, including outpatient services;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Type of survey to be conducted;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Whether the facility has special care units or off-site clinics or locations;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Whether the facility has a historical pattern of serious deficiencies or complaints; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Whether new surveyors are to accompany a team as part of their training.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Training for Hospital Surveyors

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospital surveyors should have the necessary training and experience to conduct a hospital survey. Attendance at a Basic Hospital Surveyor Training Course is suggested. New surveyors may accompany the team as part of their training prior to completing the Basic Hospital Surveyor Training Course.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Team Coordinator

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The survey is conducted under the leadership of a team coordinator. The SA (or the RO for Federal teams) should designate the team coordinator. The team coordinator is responsible

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: for assuring that all survey preparation and survey activities are completed within the specified time frames and in a manner consistent with this protocol, SOM, and SA procedures. Responsibilities of the team coordinator include:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Scheduling the date and time of survey activities;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Acting as the spokesperson for the team;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Assigning staff to areas of the hospital or tasks for the survey;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Facilitating time management;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Encouraging on-going communication among team members;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Evaluating team progress and coordinating daily team meetings;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Coordinating any ongoing conferences with hospital leadership (as determined appropriate by the circumstances and SA/RO policy) and providing on-going feedback, as appropriate, to hospital leadership on the status of the survey;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Coordinating Task 2, Entrance Conference;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Facilitating Task 4, Preliminary Decision Making;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Coordinating Task 5, Exit Conference; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Coordinating the preparation of the Form CMS-2567.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Task 1 - Off-Site Survey Preparation

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Objective

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The objective of this task is to analyze information about the provider in order to identify areas of potential concern to be investigated during the survey and to determine if those areas, or any special features of the provider (e.g., provider-based clinics, remote locations, satellites, specialty units, PPS-exempt units, services offered, etc.) require the addition of any specialty surveyors to the team. Information obtained about the provider will also allow the SA (or the RO for Federal teams) to determine survey team size and composition, and to develop a preliminary survey plan. The type of provider information needed includes:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Information from the provider file (to be updated on the survey using the Hospital/CAH Medicare Database Worksheet), such as the facility's ownership, the type(s) of services offered, any prospective payment system (PPS) exclusion(s), whether the facility is a provider of swing-bed services, and the number, type and location of any off-site locations;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Previous Federal and state survey results for patterns, number, and nature of deficiencies, as well as the number, frequency, and types of complaint investigations and the findings;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Information from CMS databases available to the SA and CMS. Note the exit date of the most recent survey;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Waivers and variances, if they exist. Determine if there are any applicable survey directive(s) from the SA or the CMS Regional Office (RO); and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Any additional information available about the facility (e.g., the hospital's Web site, any media reports about the hospital, etc).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Off-Site Survey Preparation Team Meeting

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The team should prepare for the survey offsite so they are ready to begin the survey immediately upon entering the facility. The team coordinator should arrange an off-site preparation meeting with as many team members as possible, including specialty surveyors. This meeting may be a conference call if necessary.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: During the meeting, discuss at least the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Information gathered by the team coordinator;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Significant information from the CMS databases that are reviewed;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Update and clarify information from the provider file so a surveyor can update the Medicare database using the "Hospital/CAH Medicare Database Worksheet," Exhibit 286;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Layout of the facility (if available);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Preliminary team member assignments;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Date, location and time team members will meet to enter the facility;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The time for the daily team meetings; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Potential date and time of the exit conference.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Gather copies of resources that may be needed. These may include:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Medicare Hospital CoP and Interpretive Guidelines (Appendix A);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Survey protocol and modules;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Immediate Jeopardy (Appendix Q);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Responsibilities of Medicare Participating Hospitals in Emergency Cases (Appendix V);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Hospital Swing-Bed Regulations and Interpretive Guidelines (Appendix T);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Hospital/CAH Medicare Database Worksheet, Exhibit 286;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Exhibit 287, Authorization by Deemed Provider/Supplier Selected for Accreditation Organization Validation Survey; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Worksheets for swing-bed, PPS exclusions, and restraint/seclusion death reporting.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Task 2 - Entrance Activities

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Objectives

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The objectives of this task are to explain the survey process to the hospital and obtain the

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: information needed to conduct the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Procedures

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Arrival

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The entire survey team should enter the hospital together. Upon arrival, surveyors should present their identification. The team coordinator should announce to the Administrator, or whoever is in charge, that a survey is being conducted. If the Administrator (or person in charge) is not onsite or available (e.g., if the survey begins outside normal daytime Monday-Friday working hours), ask that they be notified that a survey is being conducted. Do not delay the survey because the Administrator or other hospital staff is/are not on site or available.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Entrance Conference

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The entrance conference sets the tone for the entire survey. Be prepared and courteous, and make requests, not demands. The entrance conference should be informative, concise, and brief; it should not utilize a significant amount of time. Conduct the entrance conference with hospital administrative staff that is available at the time of entrance. During the entrance conference, the Team Coordinator should address the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Explain the purpose and scope of the survey;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Briefly explain the survey process;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Introduce survey team members, including any additional surveyors who may join the team at a later time, the general area that each will be responsible for, and the various documents that they may request;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Clarify that all hospital areas and locations, departments, and patient care settings under the hospital provider number may be surveyed, including any contracted patient care activities or patient services located on hospital campuses or hospital provider based locations;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Explain that all interviews will be conducted privately with patients, staff, and visitors, unless requested otherwise by the interviewee;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Discuss and determine how the facility will ensure that surveyors are able to obtain the photocopies of material, records, and other information as they are needed;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Obtain the names, locations, and telephone numbers of key staff to whom questions should be addressed;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Discuss the approximate time, location, and possible attendees of any meetings to be held during the survey. The team coordinator should coordinate any meetings with facility leadership; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Propose a preliminary date and time for the exit conference.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: During the entrance conference, the Team Coordinator will arrange with the hospital administrator, or available hospital administrative supervisory staff if he/she is unavailable to obtain the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · A location (e.g., conference room) where the team may meet privately during the survey;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · A telephone for team communications, preferably in the team meeting location;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · A list of current inpatients, providing each patient's name, room number, diagnosis(es), admission date, age, attending physician, and other significant information as it applies to that patient. The team coordinator will explain to the hospital that in order to complete the survey within the allotted time it is important the survey team is given this information as soon as possible, and request that it be no later than 3 hours after the request is made. SAs may develop a worksheet to give to the facility for obtaining this information;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · A list of department heads with their locations and telephone numbers;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · A copy of the facility's organizational chart;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The names and addresses of all off-site locations operating under the same provider number;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The hospital's infection control plan;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · A list of employees;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The medical staff bylaws and rules and regulations;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · A list of contracted services; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · A copy of the facility's floor plan, indicating the location of patient care and treatment areas;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Arrange an interview with a member of the administrative staff to complete the Hospital/CAH Medicare Database Worksheet that will be used to update the provider's file in the Medicare database. The worksheet may not be given to hospital personnel for completion.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospital Tours

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Guided tours of the hospital are not encouraged and should be avoided. While a tour of a small facility may take place in less than one-man hour, a tour of a large facility could consume several man hours of allocated survey time and resources that are needed to conduct the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Initial On-Site Team Meeting

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: After the conclusion of the Entrance Conference, the team will meet in order to evaluate information gathered, and modify surveyor assignments, as necessary. Do not delay the continuation of the survey process waiting for information from the provider, but adjust survey activities as necessary. During the on-site team meeting, team members should:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review the scope of hospital services;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Identify hospital locations to be surveyed, including any off-site locations;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Add survey protocol modules and adjust surveyor assignments, as necessary, based on new information;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Discuss issues such as change of ownership, sentinel events, construction activities,

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: and disasters, if they have been reported;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Make an initial patient sample selection (The patient list may not be available immediately after the entrance conference, therefore the team may delay completing the initial patient sample selection a few hours as meets the needs of the survey team); and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Set the next meeting time and date.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Sample Size and Selection

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: To select the patient sample, review the patient list provided by the hospital and select patients who represent a cross-section of the patient population and the services provided. Patient logs (ER, OB, OR, restraint, etc) may be used in conjunction with the patient list to assure the sample is reflective of the scope of services provided by the hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Whenever possible and appropriate, select patients who are in the facility during the time of survey (i.e., open records). Open records allow surveyors to conduct a patient-focused survey and enable surveyors to validate the information obtained through record reviews with observations and patient and staff interviews. There may be situations where closed records are needed to supplement the open records reviewed (e.g., too few open records, complaint investigation, etc), surveyors should use their professional judgment in these situations and select sample that will enable them to make compliance determinations. If it is necessary to remove a patient from the sample during the survey, (e.g., the patient refuses to participate in an interview), replace the patient with another who fits a similar profile. This should be done as soon as possible in the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Select the number of patient records for review based on the facility's average daily census. The sample should be at least 10 percent of the average daily census, but not fewer than 30 inpatient records. For small general hospitals (this reduction does not apply to surgical or other specialty hospitals) with an average daily census of 20 patients or less, the sample should not be fewer than 20 inpatient records, provided that number of records is adequate to determine compliance. Within the sample, select at least one patient from each nursing unit (e.g., med/surg, ICU, OB, pediatrics, specialty units, etc). In addition to the inpatient sample, select a sample of outpatients in order to determine compliance in outpatient departments, services, and locations. The sample size may be expanded as needed to assess the hospital's compliance with the CoP.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If a complaint is being investigated during the survey, include patients who have been identified as part of the complaint in the sample. Issues or concerns identified through complaints may be an area of focus when selecting the patient sample.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Give each patient in the sample a unique identifier. Appropriate identifiable information should be kept on a separate identifier list. Do not use medical record numbers, Social Security numbers, care unit or billing record numbers to identify patients.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: To conduct an initial survey of a hospital there must be enough inpatients currently in the hospital and patient records (open and closed) for surveyors to determine whether the hospital can demonstrate compliance with all the applicable CoP. The number of current and discharged inpatients and outpatients in relation to the complexity of care provided to patients and the length of stay of those patients needs to be large enough for surveyors to evaluate the manner and degree to which the hospital satisfies all the standards within each CoP including any CoP applying to optional services offered by the hospital. Utilize the same sample size and selection methods as previously discussed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Task 3 - Information Gathering/Investigation

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Objective

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The objective of this task is to determine the hospital's compliance with the Medicare CoP through observations, interviews, and document review.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Guiding Principles

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Focus attention on actual and potential patient outcomes, as well as required processes.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Assess the care and services provided, including the appropriateness of the care and services within the context of the regulations.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Visit patient care settings, including inpatient units, outpatient clinics, anesthetizing locations, emergency departments, imaging, rehabilitation, remote locations, satellites, etc.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Observe the actual provision of care and services to patients and the effects of that care, in order to assess whether the care provided meets the needs of the individual patient.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Use the interpretive guidelines and other published CMS policy statements to guide the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Use Appendix Q for guidance if Immediate Jeopardy is suspected.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Procedures

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Locations

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For hospitals with either no or a small number of off-campus provider-based locations, survey all departments, services, and locations that bill for services under the hospital's provider number and are considered part of the hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For hospitals with many provider-based locations survey:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · All hospital departments and services at the primary hospital campus and on the campuses of other remote locations of the hospital;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · All satellite locations of the hospital;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · All inpatient care locations of the hospital;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · All out-patient surgery locations of the hospital;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · All locations where complex out-patient care is provided by the hospital; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Select a sample of each type of other services provided at additional provider- based locations.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: On any Medicare hospital survey, contracted patient care activities or patient services (such as dietary services, treatment services, diagnostic services, etc.) located on hospital campuses or hospital provider based locations should be surveyed as part of the hospital for compliance with the conditions of participation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: During the Survey

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Observe what activities are taking place and assess the CoP that represent the scope and complexity of the patient care services located at each location, as well as, any other CoP that apply to those locations. Expand the survey activities as necessary.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The SA and surveyors have discretion whether to allow, or to refuse to allow, facility personnel to accompany the surveyors during a survey. Surveyors should make a decision whether to allow facility personnel to accompany them based on the circumstances at the time of the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: . The team should meet at least daily in order to assess the status of the survey, progress of completion of assigned tasks, areas of concern, and to identify areas for additional investigations. The team meetings should include an update by each surveyor that addresses findings and areas of concern that have been identified. If areas of concern are identified in the discussion, the team should coordinate efforts to obtain additional information. Additional team meetings can be called at any time during the survey to discuss crucial problems or issues.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · All significant issues or significant adverse events must be brought to the team coordinator's attention immediately.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Maintain open and ongoing dialogue with the facility staff throughout the survey process. Conferences with facility staff may be held in order to inform them of survey findings. This affords facility staff the opportunity to present additional information or to offer explanations concerning identified issues. Survey information must not be discussed unless the investigation process and data collection for the specific concerns is completed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Surveyors should always maintain a professional working relationship with facility staff.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Surveyors need to respect patient privacy and maintain patient confidentiality at all times during the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Surveyors should maintain their role as representatives of a regulatory agency. Although non-consultative information may be provided upon request, the surveyor is not a consultant.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Patient Review

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A comprehensive review of care and services received by each patient in the sample should be part of the hospital survey. A comprehensive review includes observations of care/services provided to the patient, patient and/or family interview(s), staff interview(s), and medical record review. After obtaining the patient's permission, observe each sample patient receiving treatments (e.g., intravenous therapy, tube feedings, wound dressing changes) and observe the care provided in a variety of treatment settings, as necessary, to determine if patient needs are met.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Observations

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Observations provide first-hand knowledge of hospital practice. The regulations and interpretive guidelines offer guidance for conducting observations. Observation of the care environment provides valuable information about how the care delivery system works and how hospital departments work together to provide care. Surveyors are encouraged to make observations, complete interviews, and review records and policies/procedures by stationing themselves as physically close to patient care as possible. While completing a chart review, for instance, it may be possible to also observe the environment and the patients, as far as care being given, staff interactions with patients, safety hazards, and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: infection control practices. When conducting observations, particular attention should be given to the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Patient care, including treatments and therapies in all patient care settings;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Staff member activities, equipment, documentation, building structure, sounds and smells;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · People, care, activities, processes, documentation, policies, equipment, etc., that are present that should not be present, as well as, those that are not present that should be present;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Integration of all services, such that the facility is functioning as one integrated whole;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Whether quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) is a facility- wide activity, incorporating every service and activity of the provider and whether every facility department and activity reports to, and receives reports from, the facility's central organized body managing the facility-wide QAPI program; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Storage, security and confidentiality of medical records.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A surveyor should take complete notes of all observations and should document: the date and time of the observation(s); location; patient identifiers, individuals present during the observation, and the activity being observed (e.g., therapy, treatment modality, etc).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A surveyor should have observations verified by the patient, family, facility staff, other survey team member(s), or by another mechanism. For example, when finding an out-dated medication in the pharmacy, ask the pharmacist to verify that the drug is out-dated. In addition, a surveyor should integrate the data from observations with data gathered through interviews and document reviews.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Surveyors must not examine patients by themselves, although in certain circumstances, in order to determine a patient's health status and whether appropriate health care is being provided, especially to ensure a patient's welfare where he/she appears to be in immediate jeopardy, it is permissible and necessary to examine the patient. After obtaining permission from the patient, the surveyor should request that a staff member of the facility examine the patient in the surveyor's presence. The health and dignity of the patient is always of paramount concern. A surveyor must respect the patient's right to refuse to be examined.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interviews

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interviews provide a method to collect information, and to verify and validate information obtained through observations. Informal interviews should be conducted throughout the duration of the survey. Use the information obtained from interviews to determine what additional observations, interviews, and record reviews are necessary. When conducting interviews, observe the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Maintain detailed documentation of each interview conducted. Document the interview date, time, and location; the full name and title of the person interviewed; and key points made and/or topics discussed. To the extent possible, document quotes from the interviewee.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Interviews with facility staff should be brief. Use a few well-phrased questions to elicit the desired information. For example, to determine if a staff member is aware of disaster procedures and his/her role in such events, simply ask, "If you smelled smoke, what would you do?"

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · When interviewing staff, begin your interviews with staff that work most closely with the patient.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Conduct patient interviews regarding their knowledge of their plan of care, the implementation of the plan, and the quality of the services received. Other topics for patient or family interview may include patient rights, advanced directives, and the facility's grievance/complaint procedure.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Interviews with patients must be conducted in privacy and with the patient's prior permission.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Use open-ended questions during your interview.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Validate all information obtained.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Telephone interviews may be conducted if necessary, but a preference should be made for in- person interviews.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Integrate the data from interviews with data gathered through observations and document reviews.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Staff interviews should gather information about the staff's knowledge of the patient's needs, plan of care, and progress toward goals. Problems or concerns identified during a patient or family interview should be addressed in the staff interview in order to validate the patient's perception, or to gather additional information.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Patient interviews should include questions specific to the patient's condition, reason for hospital admission, quality of care received, and the patients knowledge of their plan of care. For instance, a surgical patient should be questioned about the process for preparation for surgery, the patient's knowledge of and consent for the procedure, pre-operative patient teaching, post-operative patient goals and discharge plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Document Review

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Document review focuses on a facility's compliance with the CoP. When conducting a document review, document the source and date of the information obtained. When making document copies, identify the original date of the document and indicate the date and time the copies were made. Once a document review is completed, integrate the data obtained with data gathered through observations and interviews to decide if the hospital is in compliance with the CoP. Documents reviewed may be both written and electronic and include the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Patient's clinical records, to validate information gained during the interviews, as well as for evidence of advanced directives, discharge planning instructions, and patient teaching. This review will provide a broad picture of the patient's care. Plans of care and discharge plans should be initiated immediately upon admission, and be modified as patient care needs change. The record review for that patient who has undergone surgery would include a review of the pre-surgical assessment, informed consent, operative report, and pre-, inter-, and post-operative anesthesia notes. Although team members may have a specific area assigned during the survey, the team should avoid duplication of efforts during review of medical records and each surveyor should review the record as a whole instead of targeting the assigned area of concern. Surveyors should use open patient records rather than closed records, whenever possible;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Closed medical records may be used to determine past practice, and the scope or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: frequency of a deficient practice. Closed records should also be reviewed to provide information about services that are not being provided by the hospital at the time of the survey. For example, if there are no obstetrical patients in the facility at the time of the survey, review closed OB records to determine care practices, or to evaluate past activities that cannot be evaluated using open records. In the review of closed clinical records, review all selected medical records for an integrated plan of care, timelines of implementation of the plan of care, and the patient responses to the interventions.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Personnel files to determine if staff members have the appropriate educational requirements, have had the necessary training required, and are licensed, if it is required;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Credential files to determine if the facility complies with CMS requirements and State law, as well as, follows its own written policies for medical staff privileges and credentialing;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Maintenance records to determine if equipment is periodically examined and to determine if it is in good working order and if environmental requirements have been met;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Staffing documents to determine if adequate numbers of staff are provided according to the number and acuity of patients;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Policy and procedure manuals. When reviewing policy and procedure manuals, verify with the person in charge of an area that the policy and procedure manuals are current; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Contracts, if applicable, to determine if patient care, governing body, QAPI, and other CoP requirements are included.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Photocopies

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Surveyors should make photocopies of all documents needed to support survey findings. The surveyor needs access to a photocopier where he/she can make their own photocopies of needed documents. If requested by the hospital, the surveyor should make the hospital a copy of all items photocopied. All photocopies need to be dated and timed as to when photocopied, and identified such as "hospital restraint policy- 2/17/04 page 3" or "Patient # 6, progress note- 2/17/04."

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Completion of Hospital/CAH Medicare Database Worksheet

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Arrange an interview with a member of the administrative staff to update and clarify information from the provider file. The Hospital/CAH Medicare Database Worksheet will be used to collect information about the hospital's services, locations, and staffing by Medicare surveyors during hospital surveys. The worksheet will be completed by the surveyors using observation, staff interviews, and document review. The worksheet will not be given to hospital staff to complete. The worksheet is used to collect information that will later be entered into the Medicare database. During the interview clarify any inconsistencies from prior information or information gathered during the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Task 4 - Preliminary Decision Making and Analysis of Findings

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Objectives

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The general objectives of this task are to integrate findings, review and analyze all

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: information collected from observations, interviews, and record reviews, and to determine whether or not the hospital meets the Conditions of Participation found at 42 CFR Part 482 and, as appropriate, the PPS exclusionary criteria at 42 CFR Part 412 Subpart B, and the swing-bed requirements at 42 CFR 482.66. The team's preliminary decision-making and analysis of findings assist it in preparing the exit conference report. Based on the team's decisions, additional activities may need to be initiated.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Procedures

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Preparation

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Prior to beginning this Task, each team member should review his/her notes, worksheets, records, observations, interviews, and document reviews to assure that all investigations are complete and organized for presentation to the team.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Discussion Meeting

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: At this meeting, the surveyors will share their findings, evaluate the evidence, and make team decisions regarding compliance with each requirement. Proceed sequentially through the requirements for each condition appropriate to the facility as they appear in regulation. For any issues of noncompliance, the team needs to reach a consensus. Decisions about deficiencies are to be team decisions, with each member having input. The team should document their decisions, the substance of the evidence, and the numbers of patients impacted, in order to identify the extent of facility noncompliance. The team must ensure that their findings are supported by adequate documentation of observations, interviews and document reviews and includes any needed evidence such as photocopies. Any additional documentation or evidence needed to support identified non compliance should be gathered prior to the exit conference but at a minimum, prior to exiting the hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Determining the Severity of Deficiencies

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The regulations at 42 CFR 488.26 state, "The decision as to whether there is compliance with a particular requirement, condition of participation, or condition for coverage, depends upon the manner and degree to which the provider or supplier satisfies the various standards within each condition." When noncompliance with a condition of participation is noted, the determination of whether a lack of compliance is at the Standard or Condition level depends upon the nature (how severe, how dangerous, how critical, etc.) and extent (how prevalent, how many, how pervasive, how often, etc.) of the lack of compliance. The cited level of the noncompliance is determined by the interrelationship between the nature and extent of the noncompliance.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A deficiency at the Condition level may be due to noncompliance with requirements in a single standard or several standards within the condition, or with requirements of noncompliance with a single part (tag) representing a severe or critical health or safety breach. Even a seemingly small breach in critical actions or at critical times can kill or severely injure a patient, and represents a critical or severe health or safety threat.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A deficiency is at the Standard level when there is noncompliance with any single requirement or several requirements within a particular standard that are not of such character as to substantially limit a facility's capacity to furnish adequate care, or which would not jeopardize or adversely affect the health or safety of patients if the deficient practice recurred.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: When a deficient practice (noncompliance) is determined to have taken place prior to the survey and the hospital states that it has corrected the deficient practice/issue (noncompliance), issues for the survey team to consider would include:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Is the corrective action superficial or inadequate, or is the corrective action adequate

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: and systemic?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Has the hospital implemented the corrective intervention(s) or action(s)?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Has the hospital taken a QAPI approach to the corrective action to ensure monitoring, tracking and sustainability?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The survey team uses their judgment to determine if any action(s) taken by the hospital prior to the survey is sufficient to correct the noncompliance and to prevent the deficient practice from continuing or recurring. If the deficient practice is corrected prior to the survey, do not cite noncompliance. However, if the noncompliance with any requirements is noted during the survey, even when the hospital corrects the noncompliance during the survey, cite noncompliance.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: All noted noncompliance must be cited even when corrected on site during the survey. Citing noncompliance at the appropriate level is important to the integrity of the survey process. Citing too high a level is unfair to the hospital. Citing noncompliance at a level below the noted degree and manner of the noncompliance does not ensure that the hospital will develop acceptable plans of correction and implement corrective actions, and does not depict accurately whether the care provided adversely affects the health and safety of patients; and continued deficient practices may lead to adverse patient outcomes such as injury or death.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Gathering Additional Information

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If it is determined that the survey team needs additional information to determine facility compliance or noncompliance, the team coordinator should decide the best way to conduct the additional review.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Task 5 - Exit Conference

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Objective

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The general objective of this task is to inform the facility staff of the team's preliminary findings.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Prior to the Exit Conference

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The team coordinator is responsible for organization of the presentation of the exit.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The team determines who will present the findings.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If the team feels it may encounter a problem during the exit, they should contact their immediate supervisor.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Discontinuation of an Exit Conference

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: It is CMS' general policy to conduct an exit conference at the conclusion of each survey. However, there are some situations that justify refusal to continue or to conduct an exit conference. For example:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If the provider is represented by counsel (all participants in the exit conference should identify themselves), surveyors may refuse to conduct the conference if the lawyer tries to turn it into an evidentiary hearing; or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Any time the provider creates an environment that is hostile, intimidating, or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: inconsistent with the informal and preliminary nature of an exit conference, surveyors may refuse to conduct or continue the conference. Under such circumstances, it is suggested that the team coordinator stop the exit conference and call the State agency for further direction.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Recording the Exit Conference

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If the facility wishes to audio tape the conference, it must provide two tapes and tape recorders, recording the meeting simultaneously. The surveyors should take one of the tapes at the conclusion of the conference. Video taping is also permitted if it is not disruptive to the conference, and a copy is provided at the conclusion of the conference. It is at the sole discretion of the surveyor(s) to determine if video taping is permitted.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Principles

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The following general principles apply when conducting an exit conference:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The facility determines which hospital staff will attend the exit conference.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The identity of an individual patient or staff member must not be revealed in discussing survey results. Identity includes not just the name of an individual patient or staff member, but also includes any reference by which identity might be deduced.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Because of the ongoing dialogue between surveyors and facility staff during the survey, there should be few instances in which the facility is unaware of surveyor concerns or has not had an opportunity to present additional information prior to the exit conference.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Exit Conference Sequence

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The following discusses the sequence of events in conducting an exit conference.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Introductory Remarks:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: . Thank everyone for cooperation during the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Introduce all team members, mentioning any that have concluded their portion of the survey and have left the facility.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Briefly mention the reason for the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Explain that the exit conference is an informal meeting to discuss preliminary findings.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Indicate that official findings are presented in writing on the Form CMS-2567.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Ground Rules

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Explain how the team will conduct the exit conference and any ground rules.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Ground rules may include waiting until the surveyor finishes discussing each deficiency before accepting comments from facility staff.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · State that the provider will have an opportunity to present new information after the exit conference for consideration after the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Presentation of Findings

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Avoid referring to data tag numbers.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Present the findings of noncompliance, explaining why the findings are a violation. If the provider asks for the regulatory basis, provide it.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Refrain from making any general comments (e.g., "Overall the facility is very good"). Stick to the facts. Do not rank findings. Treat requirements as equal as possible.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Do not identify unmet requirements as condition or standard level. Avoid statements such as, "the condition was not met" or "the standard was not met." It is better to state "the requirement is not met."

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If immediate jeopardy was identified, explain the significance and the need for immediate correction. Follow instructions in Appendix Q.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Assure that all findings are discussed at the exit conference.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Closure

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Explain that a statement of deficiencies (Form CMS-2567) will be mailed within 10 working days to the hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Explain that the Form CMS-2567 is the document disclosed to the public about the facility's deficiencies and what is being done to remedy them. The Form CMS- 2567 is made public no later than 90 calendar days following completion of the survey. It documents specific deficiencies cited, the facility's plans for correction and timeframes, and it provides an opportunity for the facility to refute survey findings and furnish documentation that requirements are met.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Inform the facility that a written plan of correction must be submitted to the survey agency within 10 calendar days following receipt of the written statement of deficiencies.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Explain the required characteristics of a plan of correction. The characteristics include:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Corrective action to be taken for each individual affected by the deficient practice, including any system changes that must be made;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The position of the person who will monitor the corrective action and the frequency of monitoring;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Dates each corrective action will be completed;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The administrator or appropriate individual must sign and date the Form CMS-2567 before returning it to the survey agency; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The submitted plan of correction must meet the approval of the State agency, or in some cases the CMS Regional Office for it to be acceptable.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If the exit conference was audio or video taped, obtain a copy of the tape in its entirety before leaving the facility.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: All team members should leave the facility together immediately following the exit conference. If the facility staff provides further information for review, the team coordinator should decide the best way to conduct the further review. It is usually prudent for at least two individuals to remain.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Task 6 - Post-Survey Activities

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Objective

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The general objective of this task is to complete the survey and certification requirements, in accordance with the regulations found at 42 CFR Part 488.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Procedures

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Each State agency and Federal Regional Office should follow directives in the State Operations Manual. The procedures include:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Timelines for completing each step of the process;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Responsibilities of the team coordinator and other team members to complete the Form CMS-2567, "Statement of Deficiencies," following the "Principles of Documentation";

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Notification to the facility staff regarding survey results;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Additional survey activities based on the survey results (e.g., revisit, forwarding documents to the Regional Office for further action/direction);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Completion of "Hospital Restraint/Seclusion Death Reporting Worksheet," as appropriate;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Compilation of documents for the provider file;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Signed Authorization by Deemed Provider/Supplier Selected for Accreditation Organization Validation Survey is forwarded to RO; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Enter the information collected on the Hospital/CAH Medicare Database Worksheet into the Medicare database.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Plan of Correction

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Regulations at 42 CFR 488.28(a) allow certification of providers with deficiencies at the Standard or Condition level "only if the facility has submitted an acceptable plan of Correction [POC] for achieving compliance within a reasonable period of time acceptable to the Secretary." Failure to submit a POC may result in termination of the provider agreement as authorized by 42 CFR 488.28(a) and §489.53(a)(1). After a POC is submitted, the surveying entity makes the determination of the appropriateness of the POC.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Psychiatric Hospital Survey Module

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Background

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: State survey agencies are given the responsibility for conducting surveys of psychiatric hospitals to determine compliance with the two special conditions of participation. However, most are not staffed with the personnel with the psychiatric expertise necessary to conduct the surveys. In light of this, CMS has contracted out this function for many years,

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: and a panel of contracted psychiatric consultants has conducted the majority of surveys of psychiatric hospitals.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: General Procedures

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: When conducting a validation survey or other full survey of a psychiatric hospital using the hospital A-tags located in Appendix A of the SOM, the SA is also expected to conduct a review of the two special conditions of participation for psychiatric hospitals if:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The State survey agency has the expertise (i.e., at a minimum a Masters prepared psychiatric nurse or an RN with inpatient psychiatric nursing experience) to serve on the team. The surveyors should conduct the survey of the two special conditions as outlined in Appendix AA of the State Operations Manual.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospital Swing-Bed Survey Module

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: When conducting a full survey of an accredited or unaccredited hospital that has swing-bed approval, conduct a survey of the hospital swing-bed requirements found at 42 CFR 482.66. These requirements, as well as interpretive guidelines, are found in Appendix T of the SOM. An optional survey worksheet, also found in Appendix T, may be used.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Background

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Swing-bed patients are hospital patients who are situated in the hospital but for whom the hospital is receiving reimbursement for skilled nursing services, as opposed to acute-care reimbursement. The reference to swing-bed is a patient care and reimbursement status and has no relationship to geographic location in the facility. The patient may be in acute-care status one day and change to swing-bed status the next day. It is not necessary for the patient to change location in the hospital when the reimbursement status changes, but moving to a different location is allowed. A 3-day qualifying stay for the same spell of illness in any hospital or critical access hospital (CAH) is required prior to admission to swing-bed status. The 3-day qualifying stay does not need to be from the same facility as the swing-bed admission.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Regulatory Authority and Requirements for Hospital Providers of Extended Care Services ("Swing-beds")

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospital swing-bed care is regulated by both the hospital requirements at 42 CFR Part 482 (reprinted at Appendix A of the SOM) and the swing-bed requirements at 42 CFR 482.66 (also in Appendix T, along with an optional surveyor worksheet). The actual swing-bed survey requirements are referenced in the Medicare Nursing Home requirements at 42 CFR Part 483.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Section 1883 of the Act authorizes payment under Medicare for post-hospital SNF services provided by any hospital that meets certain requirements. By regulation, the Secretary has specified these requirements at 42 CFR 482.66:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The hospital has a Medicare provider agreement;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The facility has fewer than 100 hospital beds, excluding beds for newborns and beds in intensive care type inpatient units;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The hospital is located in a rural area. This includes all areas not delineated as "urbanized" areas by the Census Bureau, based on the most recent census;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The hospital does not have in effect a 24-hour nursing waiver granted under 42 CFR §488.54(c);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The hospital has not had a swing-bed approval terminated within the two years previous to application; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The hospital meets the swing-bed CoP on Resident Rights; Admission, Transfer, and Discharge Rights; Resident Behavior and Facility Practices; Patient Activities; Social Services; Discharge Planning; Specialized Rehabilitative Services; and Dental Services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Activities Conducted Prior to Swing-Bed Survey

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Prior to conducting the swing-bed survey, verify the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The hospital continues to be located in a rural census tract;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The hospital does not have a 24-hour nursing waiver in place; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The hospital's swing-bed approval is in effect and has not been terminated within the two previous years.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: In conducting the survey, verify that the hospital has fewer than 100 hospital beds, excluding beds for newborns and beds in intensive care units. A hospital licensed for more than 100 beds may be eligible for swing-bed approval if it utilizes and staffs for fewer than 100 beds. Count the staffed beds in each nursing unit. Do not count beds in recovery rooms, intensive care units, operating rooms, newborn nurseries or stretchers in emergency departments.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Assess the hospital's compliance with the swing-bed requirements at 42 CFR 482.66, found in Appendix T of the SOM, and the hospital survey methods contained in the hospital survey protocol. Swing-bed requirements apply to any patient discharged from the hospital and admitted to a swing-bed for skilled nursing services. The requirements for acute-care hospitals also apply.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If swing-bed patients are present during the on-site inspection, conduct an open record review and an environmental assessment. Include patient interviews and observations of care and services. However, if no swing-bed patients are present during the on-site inspection, review two closed records for compliance with swing-bed requirements. In all cases, review policies, procedures, and contracted services to assure that the hospital has the capability to provide the services needed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: It is important for surveyors to maintain on-going documentation of their findings during the course of the survey for later reference. Surveyors may use the optional swing-bed worksheet as a note-taking tool to document and record their findings on the survey.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Exit Conference

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Any findings of noncompliance may be discussed during the time of the hospital exit conference.

content: Post-Survey Activities

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The findings for swing-bed deficiencies must be documented on a separate Form CMS- 2567, even though the swing-bed survey is being conducted simultaneously with the hospital survey.

content: · "spouse" means an individual who is married to another individual as a result of marriage lawful where it was entered into, including a lawful same-sex marriage, regardless of whether the jurisdiction where the hospital is located, or in which the spouse lives, permits such marriages to occur or recognizes such marriages.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: . "marriage" means a marriage lawful where entered into, including a lawful same- sex marriage, regardless of whether the jurisdiction where the hospital is located, or in which the spouse lives, permits such marriages to occur or recognizes such marriages;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · "family" includes, but is not limited to, an individual's "spouse" (see above); and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · "relative" when used as a noun, includes, but is not limited to, an individual's "spouse" (see above).
