title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.26(b) Standard: Safety for Patients and Personnel

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The radiologic services, particularly ionizing radiology procedures, must be free from hazards for patients and personnel.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.26(b)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must adopt and implement radiologic services policies and procedures that provide safety for affected patients and hospital personnel and which are consistent with accepted professional standards for radiologic services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Ionizing Radiology Procedures

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Radiologic services modalities that use ionizing radiation have increased the ability to detect disease or injury early enough for a medical problem to be managed, treated, or cured. When applied and performed appropriately, these radiologic studies or procedures can maintain or improve health and save lives.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: X-ray energy used in radiologic services also has a potential to harm living tissue. The most significant risks are:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Cataracts and skin damage, but only at very high levels of radiation exposure; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · An increase in the possibility that a person exposed to x-ray energy will develop cancer later in life. The risk of developing cancer from radiologic services radiation exposure is generally very small, and it depends on at least three factors-the amount of the radiation dose, the age of the person exposed, and the sex of the person exposed:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The lifetime risk of cancer increases the larger the dose and the more x-ray studies or procedures a patient undergoes;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The lifetime risk of cancer is larger for a patient who received x-rays at a younger age than for one who receives them at an older age; and.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Women are at a somewhat higher lifetime risk than men for developing radiation- associated cancer after receiving the same exposures at the same ages.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: MRI:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: MRIs are useful when a soft tissue injury or disease process is suspected and are generally considered at low risk of causing harm to patients or staff. However, they also are not entirely risk-free. Potential risks include projectile risk of magnetic objects being sucked into the main magnet, thermal injury and burns, adverse effects on devices and leads implanted in patients, and hearing damage.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Provision of services in accordance with professionally approved standards for safety

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: All radiological services provided by the hospital, including both diagnostic and, if offered, therapeutic services, must be provided in accordance with acceptable standards of practice, including standards for safety.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Professionally approved standards include maintaining compliance with applicable Federal and State laws and regulations governing radiological services, including, but not limited to, facility licensure and/or certification requirements.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Professionally approved standards also include the recommendations or guidelines promulgated by expert governmental agencies, such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, as well as those issued by nationally recognized professional organizations, such as the American Medical Association, American College of Radiology, Radiological Society of North America, The Alliance for Radiation Safety in Pediatric Imaging, American Society of Radiologic Technologists, the American College of Cardiology, the American College of Neurology, the American College of Physicians, etc.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Generally, there are different standards for different imaging modalities used to provide radiologic services; there may also be different standards for diagnostic versus therapeutic uses, as well as for pediatric versus adult patients, etc. For example, the American College of Radiology has separate diagnostic radiology guidance documents for general radiology, CT, MRI, and ultrasound, among others. The hospital must be able to document the source

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: standards that form the basis for its policies and procedures for each of its radiologic services modalities and/or settings. For example, if one organization's standards are used for mammography services, another's for CT services, another's for MRI, and another's for pediatric X-rays, this must be clearly indicated.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: In order to ensure safety and freedom from hazards, the hospital's radiologic services policies and procedures must include, but are not limited to, provisions addressing the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · For ionizing radiation services, application of the fundamental principle of As Low as Reasonably Achievable or ALARA, which is defined by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) as "A principle of radiation protection philosophy that requires that exposures to ionizing radiation be kept as low as reasonably achievable, economic and social factors being taken into account. The protection from radiation exposure is ALARA when the expenditure of further resources would be unwarranted by the reduction in exposure that would be achieved." (Federal Guidance Report No. 14, Radiation Protection Guidance for Diagnostic and Interventional X-ray Procedures, p. 100, November, 2014) Although CMS does not interpret or enforce EPA guidance, the ALARA principle is considered an accepted standard of practice for ionizing radiation services to which hospitals must adhere.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Written protocols developed or approved by the radiologist responsible for the radiologic services, in conjunction with other qualified radiologic services personnel (e.g., a medical physicist, radiologic technologists, patient safety officers, etc.) designed to ensure that diagnostic studies and therapeutic procedures are routinely performed in a safe manner, utilizing parameters and specifications that are appropriate to the ordered study/procedure. The hospital must ensure that protocols for the various types of ionizing radiation diagnostic or therapeutic imaging modalities are designed to minimize the amount of radiation while maximizing the yield and producing diagnostically acceptable image quality. Existing protocols must be reviewed periodically and updated as needed. The rationale and details for changes to technical parameters must be documented.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For Information Only - Not Required/Not to be Cited

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospitals are encouraged to follow the recommendation in the EPA's Guidance Report No. 14 concerning patient radiation dosage. The report says "As the ICRP [International Commission on Radiological Protection] has stated, 'Provided that the medical exposures of patients have been properly justified and that the associated doses are commensurate with the medical purpose, it is not appropriate to apply dose limits or dose constraints to the medical exposure of patients, because such limits or constraints would often do more harm than good' (ICRP 2007b). While dose limits do not apply to medical exposures, radiation doses to patients should always be optimized. All responsible parties should always strive to minimize patient irradiation to the dose that is necessary to perform the procedure with adequate image quality. The recommendation against establishing absolute dose limits should not discourage a facility from implementing diagnostic reference levels for imaging and interventional procedures. Exceeding these levels should prompt a review of practice at the facility as a quality assurance measure. Dose notification and alert values for CT, notification levels for use during inter

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: rocedures. Exceeding these levels should prompt a review of practice at the facility as a quality assurance measure. Dose notification and alert values for CT, notification levels for use during interventional procedures, and trigger levels for follow-up after interventional procedures are also appropriate QA measures [emphasis added] ... (EPA Guidance Report No. 14, p.6)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Policies and protocols to identify patients at high risk for adverse events for whom the radiologic study or procedure might be contraindicated, e.g., pregnant women, individuals with known allergies to contrast agents, individuals with implanted devices, etc. Policies would address the steps to be taken, and by which personnel, if an order is written for a radiologic study or procedure for an individual identified in the radiologic services policies as potentially at high risk (e.g., notify the ordering physician, cancel the procedure personally, etc.).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Specific requirements related to procedures to mitigate radiation hazards are discussed in the guidance for §482.26(b)(1).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Procedures to address risks associated with modalities that do not use ionizing radiation. For example, with respect to MRI:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Measures to prevent magnetic materials from being closer than is safe to the MRI suite, per nationally recognized guidelines;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If equipment and supplies, such as fire extinguishers and oxygen tanks, are located in the MRI area, they are MR-safe, i.e., they are non-ferromagnetic;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Provision of adequate and effective hearing protection to patients, staff and others who might be in the MRI suite while the scans are taking place; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Measures to reduce the risk of thermal injuries/burns during MRI. This would include, but is not limited to, screening patients to identify those who may have metallic tattoos or metal in them, proper patient positioning, ensuring implants are MR Conditional, checking for electrically conductive materials that might be in close proximity to the patient and taking the appropriate precautions, and instructing the patient to immediately report any burning sensations experienced during the scan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Training required by personnel permitted to enter areas where radiologic services are provided.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Training and, as applicable, qualifications, required for personnel who perform diagnostic imaging studies or therapeutic procedures utilizing radiologic services equipment. This includes proper operation of equipment per manufacturer's instructions and hospital policy.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Areas where radiologic services are provided must be equipped with the necessary equipment or materials to immediately respond to potential adverse events. This could include, but is not limited to, things like a crash cart, emergency stop mechanisms, cleaning and decontamination agents if applicable, etc.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For Information Only - Not Required/Not to be Cited

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospitals are encouraged to also address the following in their Radiologic Services:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Encouraging physicians and other practitioners with privileges to order radiologic studies or procedures that utilize ionizing radiation to consider both the benefits and risks of the procedures.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Recording and tracking the dosing patients receive. There are several nationally recognized quality assurance programs designed to assist health care providers in developing and maintaining this data, including, but not limited to:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The Alliance for Safety in Pediatric Imaging (www.Imagegently.org)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The Conference of Radiation Control Program Directors

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The American College of Radiology data registry (http://nrdr.acr.org)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The Nationwide Evaluation of X-ray Trends (NEXT program)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Further, although the EPA's Guidance Report No. 14 was developed by an Interagency Working Group on Medical Radiation specifically to provide guidance to Federal facilities that use diagnostic and interventional X-ray equipment, it should also be useful to non-Federal medical facilities and hospitals are encouraged to review it. The Guidance Report addresses the following topics:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Radiation Safety Standards and General Concerns

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Structural Shielding and Door Interlock Switches

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Requesting and Performing Studies Involving X-rays

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Technical Quality Assurance

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · General Guidelines for Clinical Imaging, organized into separate sections for Medical and Dental, and further broken down by modality

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Imaging Informatics

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Recommendations for Facility Action

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Medical Physicists

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: According to the American Association of Physicists in Medicine, the practice of Medical Physics means the use of principles and accepted protocols of physics to ensure the correct quality, quantity, and placement of radiation during the performance of a radiological procedure. Hospitals are not required under the regulations to have a medical physicist on staff or under contract. However, since radiologic services are required to be free from hazards to patients and hospital personnel, hospitals must ensure that qualified personnel, whether or not they are medical physicists, develop and carry out protocols and test, calibrate, and maintain radiologic services equipment and that there is a reliable means to validate the results.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For Information Only - Not Required/Not to be Cited

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Definition of a Medical Physicist

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: An example of a definition of and qualifications for a medical physicist is provided by the American Association of Physicists in Medicine:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: "For the purpose of providing clinical professional services, a Qualified Medical Physicist (QMP) is an individual who is competent to independently provide clinical professional services in one or more of the subfields1 of medical physics. The subfields of medical physics are:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Therapeutic Medical Physics

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Diagnostic Medical Physics

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Nuclear Medicine Physics

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Medical Health Physics

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: .... A Qualified Medical Physicist meets each of the following credentials:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Has earned a master's and/or doctoral degree in physics, medical physics, biophysics, radiological physics, medical health physics, or equivalent disciplines from an accredited college or university; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Has been granted certification in the specific subfield(s) of medical physics with its associate medical health physics aspects by an appropriate national certifying body and abides by the certifying body's requirements for continuing education." http://www.aapm.org/org/default.asp

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For Information Only - Not Required/Not to be Cited

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The responsibilities of the medical physicist in a hospital may include:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · protection of the patient and others from potentially harmful or excessive radiation;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · establishment, with the approval of the Director of Radiologic Services, of adequate protocols to ensure accurate patient dosimetry;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · measurement and characterization of radiation;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · determination of delivered dose;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · promotion of procedures necessary to ensure image quality;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · development and direction of quality assurance programs; and assistance to other healthcare professionals in optimizing the balance between the beneficial and deleterious effects of radiation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospitals are also encouraged to involve a medical physicist in the calibration of the radiologic services equipment and monitoring of radiation dosage exposures to staff.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Consistent with the requirements under the Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) CoP at 42 CFR 482.21, the hospital must monitor the quality and safety of radiologic services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Examples of indicators of potential quality and safety problems could include, but are not limited to:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Improper patient preparation, such as inadequate intravenous access or lack of pre- medication, such that procedures must be cancelled or reordered;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Repeats of the same studies in the hospital for the same patient within a short time span, which may be an indicator of poor image quality; or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Diagnostic imaging studies or therapeutic procedures performed in a manner inconsistent with the applicable hospital written protocol.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Under the QAPI CoP, hospitals are required to undertake improvement activities in areas that represent high risk, high volume, or problem-prone areas. Problems identified in radiologic services may meet these criteria. In addition, adverse events related to radiologic services must be analyzed for their causes, and preventive actions must then be undertaken. Deficiencies identified related to tracking, analyzing, and addressing adverse event and quality indicator data and performance improvement activities must be cited under the applicable QAPI standards.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.26(b)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that there are written hospital policies and procedures and protocols for specific radiologic services modalities that are based on identified professionally approved standards, and which address the ALARA principle as well as the other safety and risk- reduction measures discussed in the guidance.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Ask for evidence that safety protocols are reviewed periodically and, if applicable, updated.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine if the radiologic services staff are familiar with the policies and procedures related to safety in general and specific clinical protocols.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Observe whether the policies and procedures are followed when radiologic services are delivered to patients. Ask for the protocol(s) for one or more studies/procedure(s) you observed and check if they were followed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that radiologic services staff are trained at appropriate intervals to ensure that they are operating the equipment according to manufacturer's instructions and hospital policy

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that radiologic services staff know how to respond to adverse events.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Confirm that areas where radiologic services are provided are equipped with the equipment or materials to immediately respond to an adverse event.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Ask the radiologist who supervises ionizing radiologic services how the hospital monitors the quality and safety of radiologic services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that adverse events are analyzed for their causes and that preventive actions are taken (deficiencies to be cited both here and under the applicable QAPI citation).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.26(b)(1) - Proper safety precautions must be maintained against radiation hazards. This includes adequate shielding for patients, personnel, and facilities, as well as appropriate storage, use and disposal of radioactive materials.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.26(b)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must adopt and implement written policies and procedures to ensure safety from radiation hazards. The policies and procedures must include, but are not limited to, consideration of the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Clear and easily recognizable signage identifying hazardous radiation areas;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Limitations on access to areas containing radiologic services equipment.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Appropriate use of shielding, including:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Types of personal protective shielding (e.g., lead aprons, lead gloves, protective eyewear, thyroid shields, portable individualized lead panels, stationary barriers) to be used, under what circumstances, for patients, including high-risk patients as identified in radiologic services policies and procedures, patient family members or support persons who may be needed to be with the patient during a study or procedure, and hospital personnel;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Lead and concrete barriers built into the walls and other structures of the imaging areas;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Identification and use of appropriate containers to be used for various radioactive materials, if applicable, when stored, in transport between locations within the hospital, in use, and during/after disposal.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: As a reminder, although hospitals are required to comply with applicable OSHA requirements, surveyors conducting surveys on behalf of CMS do not interpret or assess compliance with the requirements of OSHA or other Federal Agencies. content: Survey Procedures §482.26(b)(1)

content: · Verify that personal shielding, supplies and equipment are properly maintained and routinely inspected by the hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine if the proper shielding is applied to a patient who is undergoing a procedure using ionizing radiation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine if staff members appropriately extricate themselves from the immediate exposure field while performing a study or procedure using ionizing radiation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine if staff wear shielding as appropriate, per hospital policy.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.26(b)(2) - Periodic inspection of equipment must be made and hazards identified must be properly corrected.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.26(b)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must have policies and procedures in place to ensure that periodic inspections of radiology equipment are conducted, current and that problems identified are corrected in a timely manner. Equipment includes not only devices used to deliver diagnostic or therapeutic radiologic services, but also exposure meters, badges, or personal radiation monitoring devices used by staff, as well as equipment the hospital uses to inspect or calibrate devices used to deliver diagnostic or therapeutic radiologic services. The hospital must ensure that equipment is inspected in accordance with manufacturer's instructions and Federal and State laws, regulations, and guidelines, and hospital policy, as applicable. Inspections and maintenance, including correction of identified hazards, must be performed by qualified employees (e.g., medical physicists, qualified biomedical technicians, etc.) or through contractual arrangements with vendors with appropriate expertise.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospitals must follow the manufacturer's instructions as to how to inspect and maintain radiologic equipment. This includes acceptance testing (i.e., upon initial installation and after major upgrades) as well as ongoing inspection and maintenance. Documentation of preventive maintenance, quality control tests, service records, and major software/hardware upgrades must be maintained by the hospital and be readily available for inspection.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must also have a system in place, to identify and remedy equipment hazards in a timely manner. This system must include, but is not limited to: periodic and consistent calibration of equipment and, for equipment using ionizing radiation, monitoring of dosimetry parameters with phantoms to ensure that an accurate dose of radiation is delivered per the applicable protocol. In addition, hospitals must also have a system to track all modifications made to the equipment that would significantly impact the accuracy of the dosage delivered. Any adverse events related to over- or under-dosing must be identified and addressed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For Information Only - Not Required/Not to be Cited Requirements for Manufacturers Re: Instructions that Must be Made Available

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Below is an FDA summary of its requirements for manufacturers of x-ray systems to make available to purchasers and, upon request, to other parties, information related to maintenance of the following types of systems:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · For all diagnostic x-ray systems, manufacturers are required to provide to purchasers, and, upon request, to others at a cost not to exceed the cost of publication and distribution, manuals or instruction sheets that include technical and safety information (21 CFR 1020.30(h). This information must include a schedule of the maintenance necessary to keep the equipment in compliance with §§1020.30, 1020.31, 1020.32, and 1020.33 (21 CFR 1020.30(h)(1)(ii)). Manufacturers are also required to provide to assemblers, and, upon request, to others at a cost not to exceed the cost of publication and distribution, instructions for assembly, installation, adjustment, and testing of specified components of diagnostic x-ray systems adequate to ensure that the products will comply with applicable provisions of §§1020.30, 1020.31, 1020.32, and 1020.33, when assembled, installed, adjusted, and tested as directed (21 CFR 1020.30(g)).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · In addition to the requirements applicable to all diagnostic x-ray systems, there are also other requirements for specific systems:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Manufacturers of fluoroscopic x-ray systems manufactured on or after June 10, 2006 are required to provide a schedule of maintenance for any system instrumentation associated with the display of air kerma information necessary to maintain the displays of air kerma rate and cumulative air kerma within the limits of allowed uncertainty specified by 21 CFR 1020.32(k)(6). And, if the capability for user calibration of the display is provided, adequate instructions for such calibration must be supplied (21 CFR 1020.30(h)(6)(i)).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Manufacturers of computed tomography (CT) systems are required to provide a specific phantom or phantoms for quality assurance testing of specific system parameters on these systems (21 CFR 1020.33(d)(1)), and instructions on the use of the phantom(s), including a schedule of testing appropriate for the system and allowable variations for the indicated parameters (21 CFR 1020.33(d)(2)).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Manufacturers of cabinet x-ray systems are required to provide purchasers, and others, upon request, at a cost not to exceed the cost of preparation and distribution, manuals and instructions. These documents must include, among other technical and safety information, a schedule of maintenance necessary to keep the system in compliance with 21 CFR 1020.40 (21 CFR 1020.40(c)(9)(i)). Cabinet x-ray systems that are intended to be assembled or installed by the purchaser must be accompanied by instructions for assembly, installation, adjustment and testing of the cabinet x-ray adequate to ensure that the system is in compliance with the applicable provisions of 21 CFR 1020.40 when assembled, installed, adjusted and tested as directed (21 CFR 1020.40(c)(9)(ii)).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.26(b)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review the inspection records (logs) to verify that periodic inspections are conducted in accordance with Federal and State laws, regulations and manufacturer's instructions.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that inspection and maintenance activities were performed by qualified individuals

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that the maintenance logs show documentation of the calibration upon installation and after major upgrades or servicing.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review with the appropriate personnel the inspection schedule and the mechanism for identifying hazards, including accurate dosimetry determinations with phantom patients, as applicable.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine that any problems identified through the testing and maintenance program are properly corrected in a timely manner and the correction is maintained over time.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-0538 (Rev. 141, Issued: 07-10-15, Effective: 07-10-15, Implementation: 07-10-15)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.26(b)(3) - Radiation workers must be checked periodically, by the use of exposure meters or badge tests, for amount of radiation exposure.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.26(b)(3)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: This requirement applies to radiologic services personnel, as well as other hospital employees who may be regularly exposed to radiation due to working near radiation sources. This could include certain nursing and maintenance staff. The types or locations of employees who require monitoring for radiation exposure must be identified in the policies and procedures for the radiologic services developed or approved by the radiologist who supervises the services, in conjunction with the appropriately qualified radiation safety personnel. The monitoring of staff exposure must be documented by qualified personnel.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospitals are expected to educate staff who are monitored for radiation exposure about the appropriate use of the monitoring meters or badges (or through use of a "personal radiation monitoring device," which employs modern technology for the same measurement purpose). Hospitals must educate staff on the importance of tracking their radiation exposure over various timeframes, such as the most recent month and year, as well as their cumulative exposure through work. Staff also must be educated about the appropriate storage of the meters and/or badges as well as the procedures to follow if the exposure device exceeds cumulative dosage parameters specified per hospital policy. The hospital is expected to proactively monitor staff cumulative dosage and take appropriate steps if an individual staff member's cumulative dosage level exceeds parameters specified per hospital policy.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For Information Only - Not Required/Not to be Cited

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) has requirements for protecting hospital staff from radiation exposure, some of which are summarized below:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · "For information about exposure limits see: 29 CFR 1910.1096, Ionizing Radiation Standard. The standard also requires:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: . ... Every employer shall supply appropriate personnel monitoring equipment, such as film badges, pocket chambers, pocket dosimeters, or film rings, and shall require the use of such equipment [29 CFR 1910.1096(d)(2)]

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Employers shall maintain records of the radiation exposure of all employees for whom personnel monitoring is required under paragraph (d) of this section and advise each employee of his individual exposure at least yearly ...

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: See: https://www.osha.gov/SLTC/etools/hospital/clinical/radiology/radiology.html#Radiation

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: As a reminder, although hospitals are required to comply with applicable OSHA requirements, surveyors conducting surveys on behalf of CMS do not interpret or assess compliance with the requirements of OSHA or other Federal Agencies. Surveyors do assess compliance with Medicare requirements that may overlap or duplicate OSHA requirements.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.26(b)(3)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that staff being monitored have been trained about the appropriate use and storage of their badges/meters. Are staff knowledgeable about their personal radiation exposure over various timeframes?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Observe whether staff in categories or locations identified for monitoring have radiation-detecting meters or badges and that they appropriately wear and store them.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review records to verify that monitoring of staff exposure is documented.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Ask the hospital what steps it takes if staff exposure exceeds parameters established per hospital policy. Can the hospital provide examples, or, if it asserts there have been no cases in the prior 12 - 24 months, do its records support this?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.26(b)(4) - Radiologic services must be provided only on the order of practitioners with clinical privileges or, consistent with State law, of other practitioners authorized by the medical staff and the governing body to order the services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.26(b)(4)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The medical staff and the governing body determine the necessary qualifications and clinical privileges that practitioners must have to order diagnostic radiologic studies or therapeutic procedures.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For outpatient services, the governing body and medical staff may also authorize practitioners who do not have hospital privileges to order such studies or procedures, as permitted under State law. For example, a hospital may decide that it will routinely accept orders from physicians in the communities it services for outpatient diagnostic studies, regardless of whether those physicians have privileges to practice in the hospital. See the guidance for §482.54(c) for more information on requirements related to outpatient orders from practitioners who do not hold privileges to practice at the hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The order must include information for the radiologic technologist about the study or procedure to be performed, and the technologist is expected to review this information prior to implementing the order.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For Information Only - Not Required/Not to be Cited

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospitals are strongly encouraged, but not required, to develop standard formats for practitioner's orders for radiologic services that clearly document the diagnostic or therapeutic purpose of the study/procedure, as well as any other pertinent information that may lead to altering the dose of radiation, including, but not limited to:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Indication (reason) for the study/procedure

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Previous imaging studies of the body part(s) under investigation;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Additional relevant radiation exposure; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Previous adverse events (e.g., over- or underexposure of dosing, allergic reaction to contrast dye) during radiologic procedures.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: In addition, hospitals are encouraged to adopt policies to ensure that the radiation technologist performing the study/procedure confirms the order with the ordering practitioner if there are any concerns about its appropriateness.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.26(b)(4)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review medical records to determine that there is an order for all radiologic services, and that the order was dated/timed and authenticated by an authorized practitioner prior to the diagnostic study or therapeutic procedure being performed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Observe whether a radiologic technologist confirms that there is an order from an authorized practitioner and reviews information included in the order before beginning a study or procedure.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-0546 (Rev. 141, Issued: 07-10-15, Effective: 07-10-15, Implementation: 07-10-15)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.26(c) - Standard: Personnel

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (1) A qualified full-time, part-time or consulting radiologist must supervise the ionizing radiology services and must interpret only those radiologic tests that are determined by the medical staff to require a radiologist's specialized knowledge. For purposes of this section, a radiologist is a doctor of medicine or osteopathy who is qualified by education and experience in radiology.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.26(c)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The regulation defines a radiologist as a doctor of medicine (MD) or doctor of osteopathy (DO) who is qualified by education and experience in radiology. The medical staff must establish the specific criteria related to education and experience that must be met in order to be privileged as a radiologist in the hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Ionizing radiologic services offered throughout the hospital must be under the supervision of a radiologist, who may be part-time, full-time, or consulting. This may be accomplished in several ways, including by having one organized radiologic service under the direction of the supervising radiologist, or by the governing body ensuring a uniform approach to ionizing radiologic services that are offered in multiple, separately organized departments of the hospital which collaborate with the supervising radiologist in developing their department-specific protocols for ensuring that these services are free from hazards for patients and personnel.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The supervising radiologist, including, if applicable, a consultant who provides such supervision, must be privileged as a radiologist at the hospital. The extent of radiologic services provided by the hospital determines whether the supervising radiologist must carry out these responsibilities full or part-time.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For diagnostic radiologic services using ionizing radiation, policies and procedures must, in addition to the requirements addressed in other portions of the radiologic services CoP, identify which types of radiologic tests require interpretation by a radiologist, as opposed to another type of practitioner holding privileges; the hospital's medical staff must approve this policy.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: When interpretation of radiologic tests (studies) is provided via telemedicine, the radiologist interpreting the radiological test must be licensed and/or meet the other applicable standards that are required by State or local laws in the state where the hospital (and, therefore, the patient) is located. The requirements concerning granting of privileges to teleradiologists are addressed in the medical staff (§482.22) and governing body (§482.12) Conditions of Participation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.26(c)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review the medical staff privileging criteria for a radiologist. Review the credentialing and privileging file of the supervising radiologist to verify that he or she meets the qualifications established by the medical staff and has been granted privileges as a radiologist.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If the supervising radiologist is a part-time employee or consultant, ask him/her how much time/week is spent on supervising ionizing radiologic services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Is there any evidence of problems within the radiologic services that suggest lack of supervision?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine whether the medical staff has reviewed and approved a policy identifying the types of diagnostic radiologic tests (studies) that require interpretation by a radiologist. Review records to determine that a radiologist interprets those tests (studies) that have been designated.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-0547 (Rev. 141, Issued: 07-10-15, Effective: 07-10-15, Implementation: 07-10-15)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.26(c)(2) - Only personnel designated as qualified by the medical staff may use the radiologic equipment and administer procedures.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.26(c)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The medical staff must develop policies, consistent with State law, that govern the designation of all personnel who are qualified to use the radiologic equipment and perform diagnostic or therapeutic studies or procedures. Qualifications must include appropriate training and demonstrated competence in the use of equipment and administration of procedures prior to being designated as qualified. Only designated individuals may use the equipment and perform studies or procedures.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The use of the radiologic equipment includes, but is not limited to, functions such as operating the equipment according to the manufacturer's instructions and hospital policy, and interfacing with specialized technology as needed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: In addition to a radiologist, and although not specifically mentioned in the regulations, radiologic technologists are typically involved in the delivery of radiologic services in a

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: hospital. Radiologic technologists are medical personnel who typically perform diagnostic imaging examinations and administer radiation therapy treatments, as permitted under State law. They are educated in anatomy, patient positioning, examination techniques, equipment protocols, radiation safety, radiation protection, and basic patient care. All radiologic technologists using radiologic equipment or performing studies/procedures must be designated to do so.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Personnel also need to know how to respond to adverse events that may occur during a radiologic study or procedure.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospitals are expected to regularly reassess staff competency and to provide periodic training needed to keep staff skills up-to-date. The hospital must document training completion dates and evidence of satisfactory competence. Staff that complete training but cannot demonstrate satisfactory competence must not be permitted to use radiologic equipment and/or administer procedures.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.26(c)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that the medical staff established criteria for personnel who use radiologic services equipment and perform studies or procedures.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine which staff are using which pieces of radiological equipment. Review their personnel folders to determine if they meet the qualifications established by the medical staff for the tasks they perform.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that radiologic services staff are periodically trained and reassessed for competence to ensure that they are operating the equipment according to manufacturer instructions and hospital policy and know how to respond to adverse events related to their use of the equipment.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-0553 (Rev. 141, Issued: 07-10-15, Effective: 07-10-15, Implementation: 07-10-15)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.26(d) Standard: Records

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Records of radiologic services must be maintained.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (1) - The radiologist or other practitioner who performs radiology services must sign reports of his or her interpretations.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (2) - The hospital must maintain the following for at least 5 years:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) Copies of reports and printouts.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) Films, scans, and other image records, as appropriate.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.26(d)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must maintain records for all radiologic procedures performed. At a minimum, the records must include the orders for the services, copies of reports and printouts, and any films, scans, digital or other image records, as appropriate.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Radiology films, image records, scans, digital files, reports, and printouts must be secure and properly stored for at least five years. If State law requires a longer period, the hospital must comply, but surveyors do not assess compliance with State law requirements as part of the Federal survey. Patient radiologic services records are considered patient medical records and the hospital must comply with the requirements of the medical records CoP (§482.24). All reports of studies must be signed by the radiologist or other authorized practitioner (in the case of studies not designated as requiring a radiologist to interpret

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: them) who reads and evaluates the findings of the study. Acceptable forms of signature include paper signatures as well as electronic signatures.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.26(d)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine whether the hospital maintains radiologic services records for at least 5 years after the study or procedure. (Assess them for compliance with the Medical Records CoP at §482.24 at the same time, but make sure to cite general medical record noncompliance under that CoP.)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Request records for all different imaging modalities furnished by the hospital, to determine if the procedure for maintaining the records is consistent among all the radiologic services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review radiologic records to determine that reports of studies are signed by the radiologist or other authorized practitioner (in the case of studies not designated as requiring a radiologist to interpret them ) who read and evaluated the findings of the study

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.27 Condition of Participation: Laboratory Services

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must maintain, or have available, adequate laboratory services to meet the needs of its patients. The hospital must ensure that all laboratory services provided to its patients are performed in a facility certified in accordance with Part 493 of this chapter.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.27

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must maintain or have available laboratory services whenever its patients need those services. The hospital may make laboratory services available directly, through contractual agreements, or through a combination of direct and contractual services. The scope and complexity of the hospital laboratory service must be adequate to meet the needs of its patients. The hospital must maintain, or have available, adequate laboratory services to meet the needs of its patients at each campus or off-campus location of the hospital. All laboratory services, whether direct or contractual, whether conducted in a lab or in another location, must be provided in accordance with Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act (CLIA) requirements. Every hospital laboratory service must be operating under a current CLIA certificate appropriate to the level of services performed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital's laboratory services, including any contracted services, must be integrated into its hospital-wide QAPI program.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Patient laboratory results and all other laboratory clinical patient records are considered patient medical records and the hospital must comply with the requirements of the Medical Records CoP.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.27

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine the total number of laboratories, the location of each laboratory, and every location where laboratory procedures are performed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that the laboratory service and all laboratory locations are integrated into the hospital-wide QAPI program.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: . If laboratory services are contracted, verify that the review of the quality of those services is integrated into the hospital-wide QAPI program.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 37, Issued: 10-17-08; Effective/Implementation Date: 10-17-08)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.27(a) Standard: - Adequacy of Laboratory Services

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must have laboratory services available, either directly or through a contractual agreement with a certified laboratory that meets requirements of Part 493 of this chapter.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.27(a)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The CLIA certification may be accomplished by having one certificate for the entire hospital's laboratory services, by having one certificate for each laboratory, or by the hospital having a mixture. Whatever the arrangement, all laboratory services must be provided in accordance with CLIA requirements and under a current CLIA certificate, even when those laboratory services take place outside of a lab.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.27(a)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine which services are provided directly by the facility and which are provided through contractual agreements.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine if the referral laboratory is CLIA certified for the appropriate test specialty.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If the hospital provides laboratory services in multiple locations, verify that all laboratory services are operating under a current CLIA certificate.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Examine records and determine if the services, including emergency services, are provided in accordance with the hospital's policies.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 37, Issued: 10-17-08; Effective/Implementation Date: 10-17-08)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.27(a)(1) - Emergency laboratory services must be available 24 hours a day.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.27(a)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must provide emergency laboratory services 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. These onsite emergency services may be provided directly by the hospital or through onsite contracted laboratory services. Emergency lab services include collection, processing, and provision of results to meet a patient's emergency laboratory needs.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: In a hospital with multiple hospital campuses, these emergency laboratory services must be available onsite 24/7 at each campus.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The medical staff must determine which laboratory services are to be immediately available to meet the emergency laboratory needs of patients who may be currently at the hospital or those patients who may arrive at the hospital in an emergency condition. The emergency laboratory services (procedures, tests, personnel) available should reflect the scope and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: complexity of the hospital's operation and be provided in accordance with Federal and State law, regulations and guidelines and acceptable standards of practice.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: At a hospital with off-campus locations the medical staff must determine which, if any, laboratory services must be immediately available to meet the emergency laboratory needs of the patients who are likely to seek care at each off-campus location. The emergency laboratory services available must reflect the scope and complexity of the hospital's operations at the location and be provided in accordance with Federal and State law, regulations and guidelines and acceptable standards of practice. The services must be available during the hours of operation of that location.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.27(a)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Review the written description of the emergency laboratory services. Review records (including accession records, worksheets, and test reports) to verify the 24-hour availability of emergency services and that those services are provided when required.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 37, Issued: 10-17-08; Effective/Implementation Date: 10-17-08)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.27(a)(2) - A written description of services provided must be available to the medical staff.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.27(a)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify the existence of a written description of the laboratory services provided, including those furnished on routine and stat basis (either directly or under an arrangement with an outside facility).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that the description of services is accurate and current.

content: §482.27(a)(3) - The laboratory must make provision for proper receipt and reporting of tissue specimens.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.27(a)(3)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The laboratory must have written instructions for the collection, preservation, transportation, receipt, and reporting of tissue specimen results.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.27(a)(3)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Review tissue records (accession records, worksheets, and test reports) to determine whether the laboratory follows the written protocol.

CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.27(a)(4) - The medical staff and a pathologist must determine which tissue specimens require a macroscopic (gross) examination and which require both macroscopic and microscopic examinations.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.27(a)(4)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Laboratory written policies, approved by the medical staff and a pathologist, must state which tissue specimens require a macroscopic examination and which tissue specimens require both macroscopic and microscopic examination.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.27(a)(4)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that the hospital has a written policy for examination requirements.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review the written policies and tissue reports to assure that tissue specimens are examined in accordance with the written policies.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that the policies are in accordance with these requirements and other Federal and State laws, regulations, and guidelines.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.27(b) Standard: - Potentially Infectious Blood and Blood Components

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (1)Potentially human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infectious blood and blood components. Potentially HIV infectious blood and blood components are prior collections from a donor -

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) Who tested negative at the time of donation but tests reactive for evidence of HIV infection on a later donation;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) Who tests positive on the supplemental (additional, more specific) test or other follow-up testing required by FDA; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (iii) For whom the timing of seroconversion cannot be precisely estimated.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (2) Potentially hepatitis C virus (HCV) infectious blood and blood components. Potentially HCV infectious blood and blood components are the blood and blood components identified in 21 CFR 610.47.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (3) Services furnished by an outside blood collecting establishment. If a hospital regularly uses the services of an outside blood collecting establishment, it must have an agreement with the blood collecting establishment that governs the procurement, transfer, and availability of blood and blood components. The agreement must require that the blood collecting establishment notify the hospital --

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) Within 3 calendar days if the blood collecting establishment supplied blood and blood components collected from a donor who tested negative at the time of donation but tests reactive for evidence of HIV or HCV infection on a later donation or who is determined to be at increased risk for transmitting HIV or HCV infection;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) Within 45 days of the test, of the results of the supplemental (additional, more specific) test for HIV or HCV, as relevant, or other follow-up testing required by FDA;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (iii) Within 3 calendar days after the blood collecting establishment supplied blood and blood components collected from an infectious donor,

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: whenever records are available, as set forth at 21 CFR 610.48(b)(3).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (4) Quarantine of blood and blood components pending completion of testing. If the blood collecting establishment (either internal or under an agreement) notifies the hospital of the reactive HIV or HCV screening test results, the hospital must determine the disposition of the blood or blood component and quarantine all blood and blood components from previous donations in inventory.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) If the blood collecting establishment notifies the hospital that the result of the supplemental (additional, more specific) test or other follow-up testing required by FDA is negative, absent other informative test results, the hospital may release the blood and blood components from quarantine.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) If the blood collecting establishment notifies the hospital that the result of the supplemental (additional, more specific) test or other follow-up testing required by FDA is positive, the hospital must -

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (A) Dispose of the blood and blood components; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (B) Notify the transfusion recipients as set forth in paragraph (b)(6) of this section.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (iii) If the blood collecting establishment notifies the hospital that the result of the supplemental (additional, more specific) test or other follow-up testing required by FDA is indeterminate, the hospital must destroy or label prior collections of blood or blood components held in quarantine as set forth at 21 CFR 610.46(b)(2), 610.47(b)(2), and 610.48(c)(2).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (5) ) Recordkeeping by the hospital. The hospital must maintain --

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) Records of the source and disposition of all units of blood and blood components for at least 10 years from the date of disposition in a manner that permits prompt retrieval; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) A fully funded plan to transfer these records to another hospital or other entity if such hospital ceases operation for any reason.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (6) Patient notification. If the hospital has administered potentially HIV or HCV infectious blood or blood components (either directly through its own blood collecting establishment or under an agreement) or released such blood or blood components to another entity or appropriate individual, the hospital must take the following actions:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) Make reasonable attempts to notify the patient, or to notify the attending physician who ordered the blood or blood component and ask the physician to notify the patient, or other individual as permitted under paragraph (b)(10) of this section, that potentially HIV or HCV infectious blood or blood components were transfused to the patient and that there may be a need for HIV or HCV testing and counseling.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) If the physician is unavailable or declines to make the notification, make reasonable attempts to give this notification to the patient, legal guardian or relative.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (iii) Document in the patient's medical record the notification or attempts to give the required notification.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (7) Time frame for notification. For donors tested on or after February 20, 2008. For notifications resulting from donors tested on or after February 20, 2008 as set

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: forth at 21 CFR 610.46 and 21 CFR 610.47 the notification effort begins when the blood collecting establishment notifies the hospital that it received potentially HIV or HCV infectious blood and blood components. The hospital must make reasonable attempts to give notification over a period of 12 weeks unless --

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) The patient is located and notified; or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) The hospital is unable to locate the patient and documents in the patient's medical record the extenuating circumstances beyond the hospital's control that caused the notification timeframe to exceed 12 weeks.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (8) Content of notification. The notification must include the following information:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) A basic explanation of the need for HIV or HCV testing and counseling.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) Enough oral or written information so that an informed decision can be made about whether to obtain HIV or HCV testing and counseling.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (iii) A list of programs or places where the person can obtain HIV or HCV testing and counseling, including any requirements or restrictions the program may impose.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (9) Policies and procedures. The hospital must establish policies and procedures for notification and documentation that conform to Federal, State, and local laws, including requirements for the confidentiality of medical records and other patient information.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (10) Notification to legal representative or relative. If the patient has been adjudged incompetent by a State court, the physician or hospital must notify a legal representative designated in accordance with State law. If the patient is competent, but State law permits a legal representative or relative to receive the information on the patient's behalf, the physician or hospital must notify the patient or his or her legal representative or relative. For possible HIV infectious transfusion recipients that are deceased, the physician or hospital must inform the deceased patient's legal representative or relative. If the patient is a minor, the parents or legal guardian must be notified.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.27(b)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: This regulation requires the hospital to have a system in place to take appropriate action when notified that blood or blood components it received are at increased risk of transmitting HIV or HCV.

content: (Rev. 37, Issued: 10-17-08; Effective/Implementation Date: 10-17-08) §482.28 Condition of Participation: Food and Dietetic Services

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must have organized dietary services that are directed and staffed by adequate qualified personnel. However, a hospital that has a contract with an outside food management company may be found to meet this Condition of Participation if the company has a dietician who serves the hospital on a full-time, part-time, or consultant basis, and if the company maintains at least the minimum standards specified in this section and provides for constant liaison with the hospital medical staff for recommendations on dietetic policies affecting patient treatment.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretative Guidelines §482.28

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital's food and dietetic services must be organized, directed and staffed in such a manner to ensure that the nutritional needs of the patients are met in accordance with practitioners' orders and acceptable standards of practice.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital should have written policies and procedures that address at least the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Availability of a diet manual and therapeutic diet menus to meet patients' nutritional needs;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Frequency of meals served;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · System for diet ordering and patient trays delivery;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Accommodation of non-routine occurrences (e.g., parenteral nutrition (tube feeding), total parenteral nutrition, peripheral parenteral nutrition, change in diet orders, early/late trays, nutritional supplements, etc);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Integration of the food and dietetic service into the hospital-wide QAPI and Infection Control programs;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Guidelines for acceptable hygiene practices of food service personnel; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Guidelines for kitchen sanitation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The same standards apply whether the food and dietetic services are provided by the hospital directly, through a contractual agreement, or by off-site vendor.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must be in compliance with Federal and State licensure requirements for food and dietary personnel as well as food service standards, laws and regulations.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)

content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.28(a):

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must ensure that the specific food and dietetic services organization

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: requirements are met.
