title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.28(a)(1) - The hospital must have a full-time employee who-

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) Serves as director of the food and dietetic services;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) Is responsible for daily management of the dietary services; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (iii)Is qualified by experience or training.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.28(a)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The service director must be a full-time employee who has been granted the authority and delegated responsibility by the hospital's governing body and medical staff for the operation of the dietary services. This authority and delegated responsibility includes, the daily management of the service, implementing training programs for dietary staff, and assuring that established policies and procedures are maintained that address at least the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Safety practices for food handling;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Emergency food supplies;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Orientation, work assignments, supervision of work and personnel performance;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Menu planning, purchasing of foods and supplies, and retention of essential records (e.g., cost, menus, personnel, training records, QAPI reports, etc);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Service QAPI program.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Additionally, the service director must demonstrate, through education, experience and/or specialized training, the qualifications necessary to manage the service, appropriate to the scope and complexity of the food service operations.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.28(a)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that the director of the food and dietetic services is a full-time employee.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review the service director's job description to verify that it is position-specific and that responsibility and authority for the direction of the food and dietary service has been clearly delineated.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review the service director's personnel file to verify that he/she has the necessary education, experience, and training to manage the service, appropriate to the scope and complexity of food service operations.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 37, Issued: 10-17-08; Effective/Implementation Date: 10-17-08)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.28(a)(2) - There must be a qualified dietitian, full-time, part-time or on a consultant basis.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.28(a)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A qualified dietitian must supervise the nutritional aspects of patient care. Responsibilities of a hospital dietitian may include, but are not limited to:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Approving patient menus and nutritional supplements;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Patient, family, and caretaker dietary counseling;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Performing and documenting nutritional assessments and evaluating patient tolerance to therapeutic diets when appropriate;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Collaborating with other hospital services (e.g., medical staff, nursing services, pharmacy service, social work service, etc) to plan and implement patient care as necessary in meeting the nutritional needs of the patients;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Maintaining pertinent patient data necessary to recommend, prescribe, or modify therapeutic diets as needed to meet the nutritional needs of the patients.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Qualification is determined on the basis of education, experience, specialized training, State licensure or registration when applicable, and maintaining professional standards of practice.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If the qualified dietitian does not work full-time, and when the dietitian is not available, the hospital must make adequate provisions for dietary consultation that meets the needs of the patients. The frequency of consultation depends on the total number of patients, their nutritional needs and the number of patients requiring therapeutic diets or other nutritional supplementation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.28(a)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review the dietitian's personnel file to determine that he/she is qualified based on education, experience, specialized training, and, if required by State law, is licensed, certified, or registered by the State.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If the dietitian is not full-time, determine that the number of hours spent working is appropriate to serve the nutritional needs of the patients, and that the hospital makes adequate provisions for a qualified consultant coverage when the dietitian is not available.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.28(b) Menus must meet the needs of patients.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (1) - Individual patient nutritional needs must be met in accordance with recognized dietary practices.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.28(b)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Each hospital patient for whom the hospital is providing one or more meals or nutrition must have their nutritional needs met in a manner that is consistent with recognized dietary practices. Affected patients include all inpatients and those patients in outpatient status, including the provision of observation services, whose stay is sufficiently long that they must be fed. According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) Food and Nutrition Center the nationally recognized source for recommended dietary intakes allowances is the Institute of Medicine Food and Nutrition Board's Dietary Reference Intakes (DRIs), which are designed to provide recommended nutrient intakes for use in a variety of settings. The DRIs are a set of four reference values:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) is the average daily dietary intake of a nutrient that is sufficient to meet the requirement of nearly all (97-98%) healthy persons.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Adequate Intake (AI) for a nutrient is similar to the Estimated Safe and Adequate Daily Dietary Intakes (ESADDI) and is only established when an RDA cannot be determined. Therefore a nutrient either has an RDA or an AI. The AI is based on observed intakes of the nutrient by a group of healthy persons.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL) is the highest daily intake of a nutrient that is likely to pose no risks of toxicity for almost all individuals. As intake above the UL increases, risk increases.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Estimated Average Requirement (EAR) is the amount of a nutrient that is estimated to meet the requirement of half of all healthy individuals in the population.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: USDA provides access to an interactive DRI tool and DRI tables at http://fnic.nal.usda.gov/dietary-guidance/dietary-reference-intakes

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Meeting individual patient nutritional needs may include the use of therapeutic diets. Therapeutic diets refer to a diet ordered as part of the patient's treatment for a disease or clinical condition, to eliminate, decrease, or increase certain substances in the diet (e.g., sodium or potassium), or to provide mechanically altered food when indicated.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Patients must be assessed for their risk for nutritional deficiencies or need for therapeutic diets and/or other nutritional supplementation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Examples of patients who may have specialized dietary needs and may require a more detailed nutritional assessment include, but are not limited to:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: All patients requiring artificial nutrition by any means (i.e., enteral nutrition (tube

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: feeding), total parenteral nutrition, or peripheral parenteral nutrition);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Patients whose medical condition, surgical intervention, or physical status interferes with their ability to ingest, digest or absorb nutrients;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Patients whose diagnosis or presenting signs/symptoms indicates a compromised nutritional status (e.g., anorexia nervosa, bulimia, electrolyte imbalances, dysphagia, malabsorption, end stage organ diseases, etc.);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Patients whose medical condition can be adversely affected by their nutritional intake (e.g., diabetes, congestive heart failure, patients taking certain medications, renal diseases, etc.).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Patients who refuse the food served should be offered substitutes that are of equal nutritional value in order to meet their basic nutritional needs.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The care plan for patients identified as having specialized nutritional needs must address those needs as well as monitoring of their dietary intake and nutritional status. The methods and frequency of monitoring could include one or more of the following, as well as other methods:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Patient weight (BMI, unintended weight loss or gain)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Intake and output

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Lab values

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.28(b)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Can the dietician demonstrate how the menus meet the nutritional needs of patients. For example, does the service rely upon DRIs, including RDAs, in developing menus?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Can the dietician demonstrate patients are assessed for special nutritional needs and how the hospital assures the needs of those with specialized needs are met?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · When observing care in inpatient units (or observation units where meals are provided) ask staff how patients are assessed for nutritional needs.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: o Ask them how they monitor patients identified as having specialized needs.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: o Is there evidence that therapeutic diets are provided as ordered?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Does the sample of patient records being reviewed include patients identified with special nutritional needs? If not, ask to see records for several such patients. Determine if there is evidence of monitoring the dietary intake and nutritional status of patients identified as having special nutritional needs.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-0630 (Rev. 137, Issued: 04-01-15, Effective: 03-27-15, Implementation: 03-27-15)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.28(b)(2) - All patient diets, including therapeutic diets, must be ordered by a practitioner responsible for the care of the patient, or by a qualified dietitian or qualified nutrition professional as authorized by the medical staff and in accordance with State law governing dietitians and nutrition professionals.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.28(b)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Patient diets, including therapeutic diets, must be provided in accordance with orders from a practitioner responsible for the care of the patient, or by a qualified dietitian or qualified nutrition professional who is permitted to order diets under State law and authorized to do so by the medical staff.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Diets must be based on an assessment of the patient's nutritional and therapeutic needs and documented in the patient's medical record (including documentation about the patient's tolerance to any therapeutic diet ordered).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital's governing body may choose, when permitted under State law and upon recommendation of the medical staff, to grant qualified dietitians or qualified nutrition professionals diet-ordering privileges. In many cases State law determines what criteria an individual must satisfy in order to be a "qualified dietician;" State law may define the term to mean a "registered dietician" registered with a private organization, such as the Commission on Dietetic Registration, or State law may impose different or additional requirements. Terms such as "nutritionists," "nutrition professionals," "certified clinical nutritionists," and "certified nutrition specialists" are also used to refer to individuals who are not dieticians, but who may also be qualified under State law to order patient diets. It is the responsibility of the hospital to ensure that individuals are qualified under State law before appointing them to the medical staff or granting them privileges to order diets.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If the hospital chooses not to grant diet-ordering privileges to dietitians or other nutrition professionals, even when permitted under State law, the patient's diet must be prescribed by a practitioner responsible for the patient's care. In this situation, a dietitian or nutrition professional who does not have privileges to order diets may nevertheless assess a patient's nutritional needs and provide recommendations or consultations for patients to a practitioner responsible for the care of the patient.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.28(b)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review patient records to verify that diet orders are provided as prescribed by the practitioner(s) responsible for the care of the patient, a qualified dietitian, or qualified nutrition professional.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If diet orders are prescribed by a dietitian or other nutrition professional, review their records to verify that he or she was appointed to the medical staff with diet-ordering privileges, or was granted diet-ordering privileges without being appointed to the medical staff.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: o Ask the hospital how it determines whether the dietician/nutrition professional is qualified under state law. Review staff records to verify that dieticians/nutrition professionals demonstrate the required qualifications.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.28(b)(3) - A current therapeutic diet manual approved by the dietitian and medical staff must be readily available to all medical, nursing, and food service personnel.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.28(b)(3)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The therapeutic diet manual must be approved by the dietitian and the medical staff. The

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: publication or revision date of the approved therapeutic diet manual must not be more than 5 years old. The therapeutic diet manual (or copies of it) must be available to all medical, nursing and food service personnel.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine that the therapeutic diet manual is current, and:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: o Has been approved by both the medical staff and a qualified dietitian;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)

content: o Is in accordance with the current national standards, such as RDA or DRI;

content: o Includes the different types of therapeutic diets routinely ordered at the hospital; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: o Is consistently used as guidance for ordering and preparing patient diets.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.30 Condition of Participation: Utilization Review

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must have in effect a utilization review (UR) plan that provides for review of services furnished by the institution and by members of the medical staff to patients entitled to benefits under the Medicare and Medicaid programs.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.30

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If the hospital does not satisfy one of the exception criteria at §482.30(a), it must have a UR plan in effect which provides for review of services provided to Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.30

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The manner and degree of noncompliance with one or more of the UR standards is considered when determining whether there is condition-level compliance or non- compliance.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-0653 (Rev. 137, Issued: 04-01-15, Effective: 03-27-15, Implementation: 03-27-15)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.30(a) Standard: Applicability

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The provisions of this section apply except in either of the following circumstances:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (1) A Utilization and Quality Control Quality Improvement Organization (QIO) has assumed binding review for the hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (2) CMS has determined that the UR procedures established by the State under title XIX of the Act are superior to the procedures required in this section, and has required hospitals in that State to meet the UR plan requirements under §§456.50 through 456.245 of this chapter.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.30(a)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The regulation permits two exceptions to the requirement for a hospital UR plan: (1) where the hospital has an agreement with a QIO under contract with the Secretary to assume binding review for the hospital or; (2) where CMS has determined that UR procedures established by the State under Medicaid are superior to the UR requirements for the Medicare program and has required hospitals in that State to meet the UR requirements for the Medicaid program at 42 CFR 456.50 through 456.245.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: According to the regulation at 42 CFR 476.86(e), QIO review and monitoring activities fulfill the requirements for compliance activities of State Survey Agencies under §1861(k) of the Social Security Act (Act). The statutory requirements for utilization review at §1861(k) of the Act are reiterated in the UR CoP at 42 CFR 482.30. Therefore, a hospital meets the exception requirements of 42 CFR 482.30 if a QIO has assumed binding review for the hospital. (The hospital may not make requests for work to be performed by the QIO that goes beyond the scope of the QIO's contract with the Secretary.)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The regulation at 42 CFR 489.20(e) requires a hospital to maintain an agreement with a QIO to review the admissions, quality, appropriateness, and diagnostic information related to inpatient services for Medicare patients, if there is a QIO with a contract with CMS in the area where the hospital is located.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: CMS anticipates that most hospitals comply with the UR CoP by means of the QIO exception.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: With regard to the second exception, CMS would have to determine that UR procedures established by a State under Medicaid are superior to the UR requirements for Medicare. Currently no UR plans established by a State under Medicaid have been approved as exceeding the requirements under Medicare and required for hospital compliance with the Medicare UR CoP within that State. In the event that CMS approves a State's Medicaid UR process for compliance with the Medicare UR CoP, CMS will advise the affected State Survey Agency.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.30(a)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Surveyors are to verify either that the hospital:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Has its own UR plan in place and that it meets the regulatory requirements; or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If it does not have its own UR plan, that it has an agreement with the QIO that provides for binding UR review. Surveyors should ask to see the signed, dated agreement. If the hospital has an agreement with a QIO, it is not necessary for surveyors to assess the remaining UR standards.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: It is not necessary for SAs to conduct routine surveys for compliance with the provider agreement requirement to have a QIO agreement. However, a hospital that does not satisfy the UR CoP through either its own program or a QIO agreement may be cited for violating the UR CoP at the condition level.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 37, Issued: 10-17-08; Effective/Implementation Date: 10-17-08)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §82.30(b) Standard: Composition of Utilization Review Committee

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A UR committee consisting of two or more practitioners must carry out the UR function. At least two of the members of the committee must be doctors of medicine or osteopathy. The other members may be any of the other types of practitioners specified in §482.12(c)(1).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (1) Except as specified in paragraphs (b)(2) and (3) of this section, the UR committee must be one of the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) A staff committee of the institution;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) A group outside the institution --

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (A) Established by the local medical society and some or all of the hospitals in the locality; or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (B) Established in a manner approved by CMS.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (2) If, because of the small size of the institution, it is impracticable to have a properly functioning staff committee, the UR committee must be established as specified in paragraph (b)(1)(ii) of this section.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (3) The committee or group's reviews may not be conducted by any individual who --

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) Has a direct financial interest (for example, an ownership interest) in that hospital; or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) Was professionally involved in the care of the patient whose case is being reviewed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.30(b)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine the composition of the UR committee;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine that the governing body has delegated to the UR committee the authority and responsibility to carry out the UR function;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that small hospitals delegate the UR function to an outside group if it is impractical to have a staff committee;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Ascertain that committee members are not financially involved in the hospital (ownership of 5 percent or greater) nor participants in the development or execution of the patient's treatment plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 37, Issued: 10-17-08; Effective/Implementation Date: 10-17-08)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.30(c) Standard: Scope and Frequency of Review

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (1) The UR plan must provide for review for Medicare and Medicaid patients with respect to the medical necessity of --

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) Admissions to the institution;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) The duration of stays; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (iii) Professional services furnished including drugs and biologicals.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (2) Review of admissions may be performed before, at, or after hospital admission.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (3) Except as specified in paragraph (e) of this section, reviews may be conducted on a sample basis.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (4) Hospitals that are paid for inpatient hospital services under the prospective payment system set forth in Part 412 of this chapter must conduct review of duration of stays and review of professional services as follows:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) For duration of stays, these hospitals need review only cases that they reasonably assume to be outlier cases based on extended length of stay, as described in §412.80(a)(1)(i) of this chapter; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) For professional services, these hospitals need review only cases that they reasonably assume to be outlier cases based on extraordinarily high costs, as described in §412.80(a)(1)(ii) of this chapter.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.30(c)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Admissions may be reviewed before, during, or after hospital admission as stated in the hospital's UR plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Reviews may be conducted on a sample basis, except for reviews of extended stay cases.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: In an Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) hospital, to determine outlier review compliance, "reasonably assumes" is a good faith test. The question to ask is whether the hospital is reviewing outlier cases. In instances where there was no other review of outlier cases, the question is whether it was reasonable for the hospital not to have known that the cases were in fact outliers. Some medical judgment might be required to determine whether it is reasonable for the hospital to have assumed that a patient fell into a DRG other than the one eventually assigned by the intermediary. This would be an issue in long stay outlier cases where the hospital did not review because the hospital erroneously assumed that the patient was in a DRG under which the case would not have been an outlier.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.30(c)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Examine the UR plan and other documentation to determine that the medical necessity for Medicare and Medicaid patients is reviewed with respect to admission, duration of the stay, and the professional services furnished.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine if the hospital is reimbursed under IPPS. This requirement does not apply to IPPS excluded hospitals or units.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that in an IPPS hospital the following are being reviewed:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: o Duration of stay in cases reasonably assumed to be outlier cases; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: o Professional services in cases reasonably assumed to be outlier cases.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 37, Issued: 10-17-08; Effective/Implementation Date: 10-17-08)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.30(d) Standard: Determination Regarding Admissions or Continued Stays

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (1) The determination that an admission or continued stay is not medically necessary-

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) May be made by one member of the UR committee if the practitioner or practitioners responsible for the care of the patient, as specified of §482.12(c),

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: concur with the determination or fail to present their views when afforded the opportunity; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) Must be made by at least two members of the UR committee in all other cases.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (2) Before making a determination that an admission or continued stay is not medically necessary, the UR committee must consult the practitioner or practitioners responsible for the care of the patient, as specified in §482.12(c), and afford the practitioner or practitioners the opportunity to present their views.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (3) If the committee decides that admission to or continued stay in the hospital is not medically necessary, written notification must be given, no later than 2 days after the determination, to the hospital, the patient, and the practitioner or practitioners responsible for the care of the patient, as specified in §482.12(c);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.30(d)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: When other than a doctor of medicine or osteopathy makes an initial finding that the written criteria for extended stay are not met, the case must be referred to the committee, or subgroup thereof which contains at least one physician. If the committee or subgroup agrees after reviewing the case that admissions, or extended stay is not medically necessary or appropriate, the attending physician is notified and allowed an opportunity to present his views and any additional information relating to the patient's needs for admissions or extended stay. When a physician member of the committee performs the initial review instead of a non-physician reviewer, and he finds that admissions or extended stay is not necessary no referral to the committee or subgroup is necessary and he may notify the attending practitioner directly.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If the attending practitioner does not respond or does not contest the findings of the committee or subgroup or those of the physician who performed the initial review, then the findings are final.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If the attending physician contests the committee or subgroup findings, or if he presents additional information relating to the patient's need for extended stay, at least one additional physician member of the committee must review the case. If the two physician members determine that the patient's stay is not medically necessary or appropriate after considering all the evidence, their determination becomes final. Written notification of this decision must be sent to the attending physician, patient (or next of kin), facility administrator, and the single State agency (in the case of Medicaid) no later than 2 days after such final decision and in no event later than 3 working days after the end of the assigned extended stay period.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: There are only 5 working days in a given week. Normally these days are Monday through Friday, however, the institution has the option to establish 5 other days as working days. When a holiday falls on a working day, that day is not counted as a working day.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: In no case may a non-physician make a final determination that a patient's stay is not medically necessary or appropriate.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If, after referral of a questioned case to the committee or subgroup thereof, the physician reviewer determines that an admission or extended stay is justified, the attending physician shall be so notified and an appropriate date for subsequent extended stay review will be selected and noted on the patient's record.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Written notification of this final determination must be sent to the attending physician, the patient (or next of kin), the facility administrator and the single State agency (in the case of

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Medicaid) no later than 2 days after such final determination and in no event later than 3 working days after the end of the assigned extended stay period.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Where possible, the written notification should be received by all involved parties within the stated time period. Where appropriate and desired, verbal notification may precede written notification.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.30(d)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review a sample of "medically unnecessary" decisions involving admissions or continued stay that are not medically necessary and determine that these decisions are made by:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: o One member of the UR committee, if the practitioner(s) responsible for the patient's care concurs with the determination or fails to present his/her views. The practitioner must be one of those specified in §482.12(c), or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: o At least two members of the UR committee in all cases not qualified under the above.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review a sample of "medically unnecessary" decisions and verify that the physician or practitioners, as specified in §482.12(c), were informed of the committees expected decision and were given an opportunity to comment.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review a sample of "medically unnecessary" cases and verify that all involved parties are notified of the decision that care is medically not necessary no later than two days following the decision.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 37, Issued: 10-17-08; Effective/Implementation Date: 10-17-08) §482.30(e) Standard: Extended Stay Review

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (1) In hospitals that are not paid under the prospective payment system, the UR committee must make a periodic review, as specified in the UR plan, or each current inpatient receiving hospital services during a continuous period of extended duration.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The scheduling of the periodic reviews may --

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (i) Be the same for all cases; or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (ii) Differ for different classes of cases.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (2) In hospitals paid under the prospective payment system, the UR committee must review all cases reasonably assumed by the hospital to be outlier cases because the extended length of stay exceeds the threshold criteria for the diagnosis, as described in §412.80(a)(1)(i). The hospital is not required to review an extended stay that does not exceed the outlier threshold for the diagnosis.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (3) The UR committee must make the periodic review no later than 7 days after the day required in the UR plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.30(e)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review the facility's definition of extended stay in the UR plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that the hospital's UR plan requires a periodic review of each current Medicare/Medicaid inpatient receiving hospital services of extended duration and that the review is carried out at the specified time stated in the facility's UR plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The review may be the same for all cases or be different for different classes of care.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If the committee uses a different number of days for different diagnosis or functional categories for the period of extended stay, the surveyor must verify that there is a written list with lengths of stay designated for each diagnosis of functional category.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine if the hospital is under IPPS. Hospitals under IPPS need only review cases reasonably assumed to be outlier cases, and extended stay that exceeds the outlier threshold for the diagnosis.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review minutes of the UR committee. Determine that the periodic reviews of extended stay are carried out on or before the expiration of the stated period or no later than 7 days after the day required in the hospital's plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 137, Issued: 04-01-15, Effective: 03-27-15, Implementation: 03-27-15)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.30(f) Standard: Review of Professional Services

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The committee must review professional services provided, to determine medical necessity and to promote the most efficient use of available health facilities and services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.30(f)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: "Professional" services means the services provided by practitioners, including both physicians and non-physician practitioners.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The review includes medical necessity and efficient use of available health facilities and services. Examples of topics a committee may review are:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Availability and use of necessary services - underused, overuse, appropriate use

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Timeliness of scheduling of services - operating room, diagnostic

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Therapeutic procedures

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.30(f)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Determine that the committee performs a review of professional services.

CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.41 Condition of Participation: Physical Environment

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must be constructed, arranged, and maintained to ensure the safety of the patient, and to provide facilities for diagnosis and treatment and for special hospital services appropriate to the needs of the community.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.41

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: This CoP applies to all locations of the hospital, all campuses, all satellites, all provider- based activities, and all inpatient and outpatient locations.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital's Facility Maintenance and hospital departments or services responsible for the hospital's buildings and equipment (both facility equipment and patient care equipment) must be incorporated into the hospital's QAPI program and be in compliance with the QAPI requirements.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.41

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey of the Physical Environment CoP should be conducted by one surveyor. However, each surveyor as he/she conducts his/her survey assignments should assess the hospital's compliance with the Physical Environment CoP. The Life Safety Code survey may be conducted separately by a specialty surveyor.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 176, Issued: 12-29-17, Effective: 12-29-17, Implementation: 12-29-17)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.41(a) Standard: Buildings

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The condition of the physical plant and the overall hospital environment must be developed and maintained in such a manner that the safety and well-being of patients are assured.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.41(a)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must ensure that the condition of the physical plant and overall hospital environment is developed and maintained in a manner to ensure the safety and well-being of patients. This includes ensuring that routine and preventive maintenance and testing activities are performed as necessary, in accordance with Federal and State laws, regulations, and guidelines and manufacturer's recommendations, by establishing maintenance schedules and conducting ongoing maintenance inspections to identify areas or equipment in need of repair. The routine and preventive maintenance and testing activities should be incorporated into the hospital's QAPI plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must be constructed and maintained to ensure risks are minimized for patients as well as for employees and visitors. Hospitals are expected to demonstrate how they are addressing important safety features in accordance with nationally recognized standards. Although the following items are expected to be addressed when applicable, the list is not all-inclusive.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Accessibility

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The hospital must ensure all buildings at all locations of the certified hospital meet State and Federal accessibility standards (e.g. Office of Civil Rights requirements). The requirements apply to the interior and exterior of all buildings.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Age-related safety features

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Hospitals are expected to address safety hazards and risks related to age-related factors. Healthcare provided to neonatal, pediatric, and geriatric patients must be in accordance with nationally recognized standards. Age-related risks may include items such as security of inpatient and outpatient locations, access to medications, cleaning supplies and other hazardous materials, furniture and other medical

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: equipment, and increased chance of falls.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Security

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · To minimize the risk of unauthorized access to or inappropriate departure from secured healthcare units, hospitals must demonstrate security features in accordance with nationally recognized standards to ensure the safety of vulnerable patients. This includes, but is not limited to, patients such as newborn (e.g. infant abduction), pediatric, behavioral health, those with diminished capacity and dementia/Alzheimer's.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Access to non-clinical rooms identified as hazardous locations must be secured to prevent patient and visitor entry. Examples include electrical rooms and heat, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) rooms.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Ligature risk

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The presence of unmitigated ligature risks in a psychiatric hospital or psychiatric unit of a hospital is an immediate jeopardy situation. Additionally, this also includes any location where patients at risk of suicide are identified. Ligature risk findings must be referred to the health and safety surveyors for further evaluation and possible citation under Patients' Rights.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Weather-related exterior issues

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Although hospitals cannot address all weather-related issues, they are expected to address potential safety hazards specific to weather on both the exterior and interior locations in accordance of nationally recognized standards. Areas of risk include driveways, garages, entry points, walkways, etc.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Life Safety Code surveyors assess the use of power strips in healthcare facilities. However, the following guidance is provided as reference for healthcare surveyors as they survey physical environment along with other CoP requirements. Any observed power strip deficiencies should be conveyed to the LSC surveyors for citation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If line-operated medical equipment is used in a patient care room/area, inside the patient care vicinity:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · UL power strips would have to be a permanent component of a rack-, table-, pedestal-, or cart-mounted & tested medical equipment assembly

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Power strips providing power to medical equipment in a patient care room/area must be UL 1363A or UL 60601-1

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Power strips cannot be used for non-medical equipment

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If line-operated medical equipment is used in a patient care room/area, outside the patient care vicinity:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · UL power strips could be used for medical & non-medical equipment with precautions as described in the memo

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Power strips providing power to medical equipment in a patient care room/area must be UL 1363A or UL 60601-1

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Power strips providing power to non-medical equipment in a patient care room/area must be UL 1363

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If line-operated medical equipment is not used in a patient care room/area, inside and outside the patient care vicinity:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · UL power strips could be used with precautions

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Power strips providing power to non-medical equipment in a patient care room/area must be UL 1363. In non-patient care areas/rooms, other UL strips could be used with the general precautions.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.41(a)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Verify that the condition of the hospital is maintained in a manner to assure the safety and well-being of patients (e.g., condition of ceilings, walls, and floors, presence of patient hazards, etc.).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review the hospital's routine and preventive maintenance schedules to determine that ongoing maintenance inspections are performed and that necessary repairs are completed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Review a copy of the most recent environmental risk assessment to determine if the hospital has identified any accessibility, age-related, security, suicide and/or weather related risks or concerns. If environmental safety concerns have been identified in this assessment, what plans have been implemented by the hospital to ensure patient/staff safety?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Refer any potential power strip use deficiencies to Life Safety Code surveyors.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Communicate findings with health and safety surveyors as appropriate.

CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.41(a)(1) - There must be emergency power and lighting in at least the operating, recovery, intensive care, and emergency rooms, and stairwells. In all other areas not serviced by the emergency supply source, battery lamps and flashlights must be available.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.41(a)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must comply with the applicable provisions of the Life Safety Code, National Fire Protection Amendments (NFPA) 101, 2000 Edition and applicable references, such as, NFPA-99: Health Care Facilities, for emergency lighting and emergency power.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.41(a)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Use the Life Safety Code Survey Report Form (CMS-2786) to evaluate compliance with this item.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.41(a)(2) - There must be facilities for emergency gas and water supply.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.41(a)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must have a system to provide emergency gas and water as needed to provide care to inpatients and other persons who may come to the hospital in need of care. This includes making arrangements with local utility companies and others for the provision of emergency sources of water and gas. The hospital should consider nationally accepted references or calculations made by qualified staff when determining the need for at least water and gas. For example, one source for information on water is the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Emergency gas includes fuels such as propane, natural gas, fuel oil, liquefied natural gas, as well as any gases the hospital uses in the care of patients such as oxygen, nitrogen, nitrous oxide, etc.

content: The hospital should have a plan to protect these limited emergency supplies, and have a plan for prioritizing their use until adequate supplies are available. The plan should also address the event of a disruption in supply (e.g., disruption to the entire surrounding community).

content: §482.42 Condition of Participation: Infection Prevention and Control and Antibiotic Stewardship Programs

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must have active hospital-wide programs for the surveillance, prevention, and control of HAIs and other infectious diseases, and for the optimization of antibiotic use through stewardship. The programs must demonstrate adherence to nationally recognized infection prevention and control guidelines, as well as to best practices for improving antibiotic use where applicable, and for reducing the development and transmission of HAIs and antibiotic resistant organisms. Infection prevention and control problems and antibiotic use issues identified in the programs must be addressed in collaboration with the hospital-wide quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.43(b) Standard: Discharge Planning Evaluation

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (1) The hospital must provide a discharge planning evaluation to the patients identified in paragraph (a) of this section, and to other patients upon the patient's request, the request of a person acting on the patient's behalf, or the request of the physician.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (3) - The discharge planning evaluation must include an evaluation of the likelihood of a patient needing post-hospital services and of the availability of the services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (4) - The discharge planning evaluation must include an evaluation of the likelihood of a patient's capacity for self-care or of the possibility of the patient being cared for in the environment from which he or she entered the hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For every inpatient identified under the process required at §482.43(a) as at potential risk of adverse health consequences without a discharge plan, a discharge planning evaluation must be completed by the hospital. In addition, an evaluation must also be completed if the patient, or the patient's representative, or the patient's attending physician requests one. Unless the hospital has adopted a voluntary policy of developing an evaluation for every inpatient, the hospital must also have a process for making patients, including the patient's representative, and attending physicians aware that they may request a discharge planning evaluation, and that the hospital will perform an evaluation upon request. Hospitals must perform the evaluation upon request, regardless of whether the patient meets the hospital's screening criteria for an evaluation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: In contrast to the screening process, the evaluation entails a more detailed review of the individual patient's post-discharge needs, in order to identify the specific areas that must be addressed in the discharge plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.43(b)(4) requires that the evaluation include assessment of the patient's capacity for self-care or, alternatively, to be cared for by others in the environment, i.e., the setting, from which the patient was admitted to the hospital. In general, the goal upon discharge is for a patient to be able to return to the setting in which they were living prior to admission. This may be the patient's home in the community or residence in a nursing home. In the case of transfer from another hospital, generally the preferred goal is to return the patient to the setting from which he/she presented to the transferring hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The evaluation must consider what the patient's care needs will be immediately upon discharge, and whether those needs are expected to remain constant or lessen over time. If the patient was admitted from his/her private residence, the evaluation must include an assessment of whether the patient is capable of addressing his/her care needs through self- care. The evaluation must include assessment of whether the patient will require

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: specialized medical equipment or permanent physical modifications to the home, and the feasibility of acquiring the equipment or the modifications being made. If the patient is not able to provide some or all of the required self-care, the evaluation must also address whether the patient has family or friends available who are willing and able to provide the required care at the times it will be needed, or who could, if willing, be trained by the hospital sufficiently to provide the required care.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.43(b)(3) requires the evaluation to consider the patient's likelihood of needing post- hospital services and the availability of such services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If neither the patient nor the patient's family or informal caregiver(s) are able to address all of the required care needs, then the evaluation must determine whether there are community-based services that are available to meet the patient's needs while allowing the patient to continue living at home.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Such health care services include, but are not limited to:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Home health, attendant care, and other community-based services;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Hospice or palliative care;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Respiratory therapy;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Rehabilitation services (PT, OT, Speech, etc.);

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · End Stage Renal Dialysis services;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Pharmaceuticals and related supplies;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Nutritional consultation/supplemental diets; and/or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Medical equipment and related supplies.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: However, services may also include those that are not traditional health care services, but which may be essential to a patient's ongoing ability to live in the community, including, but not limited to:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Home and physical environment modifications;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Transportation services;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Meal services; and/or

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Household services, such as housekeeping, shopping, etc.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Some of the information related to needed services will emerge from the required evaluation of the patient's ability to receive care in the home, either as self-care or provided by someone else. All patients, even those with a high capability for self-care, are likely to require some follow-up ambulatory health care services, e.g., a post-discharge appointment with their surgeon, specialist or primary care physician, or a series of appointments for physical or occupational therapy. Some patients might have more complex care needs which nevertheless may still be met in the home setting, depending on the specific clinical needs and the services available in the patient's community.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For example, some patients require wound care that exceeds the capabilities of their family or others who act as informal caregivers. But they may be able to receive sufficient care in the home setting through a home health service, if such services are available. Some patients with chronic conditions may prefer to remain in their home and would be able to do so using available community-based services, but also require financial supports, such as Medicaid-financed home and community-based waiver services. If such supports are not immediately available at the time of discharge while an application for waiver services is pending, the evaluation should consider the availability of other short term supports that would allow the patient to be discharged home.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If the result of the evaluation is that the patient cannot receive required care if he/she returns to home, then an assessment must be made of options for transfer to another inpatient or residential health care facility that can address the patient's needs, including

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: other types of hospitals, such as rehabilitation hospitals; skilled nursing facilities; assisted living facilities; nursing homes; or inpatient hospice facilities.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If prior to the hospital admission the patient was a resident in a facility that he or she wishes to return to, such as an assisted living or nursing facility or skilled nursing facility, the evaluation must address whether that facility has the capability to provide the post-hospital care required by the patient. The post-discharge care requirements may be different than the care that was previously provided. This requires dialogue and cooperation between hospitals and post-hospital care facilities in the area served by the hospital, as well as with the physicians who provide care to patients in either or both of these settings.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Long term care facilities often express concern that hospitals discharge patients to their facilities with care needs that exceed their care capabilities, necessitating sending the patient to the emergency department for care and possible readmission. On the other hand, hospitals often express concern that long term care facilities send patients to the emergency department with ambulatory care-sensitive conditions, i.e., conditions that either do not require an acute level of care, or which could have been prevented from escalating to an acute level had appropriate primary care been provided in a timely manner.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: While hospitals cannot address these concerns in isolation, they are expected to be knowledgeable about the care capabilities of area long term care facilities and to factor this knowledge into the discharge planning evaluation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Hospitals are expected to have knowledge of the capabilities and capacities of not only of long term care facilities, but also of the various types of service providers in the area where most of the patients it serves receive post-hospital care, in order to develop a discharge plan that not only meets the patient's needs in theory, but also can be implemented. This includes knowledge of community services, as well as familiarity with available Medicaid home and community-based services (HCBS), since the State's Medicaid program plays a major role in supporting post-hospital care for many patients.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If the hospital is one with specialized services that attract a significant number of patients who will receive their post-hospital care in distant communities, the hospital is expected to take reasonable steps to identify the services that will be available to the patient.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Once the determination has been made that services will be necessary post-discharge, the team must then determine availability of those services or identify comparable substitutions. Included in the evaluation is coordination with insurers and other payors, including the State Medicaid agency, as necessary to ensure resources prescribed are approved and available.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For Information- Not Required/Not to be Cited

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Although not required under the regulations, hospitals would be well advised to develop collaborative partnerships with post-hospital care providers to improve care transitions of care that might support better patient outcomes. This includes not only skilled nursing facilities and nursing facilities, but also providers of community-based services. For example, Centers for Independent Living (CIL) and Aging and Disability Resource Centers (ADRC) are resources for community-based services and housing available to persons with disabilities and older adults. Hospitals can find local CIL's at http://www.ilru.org/html/publications/directory/index.html and ADRC's and other resources at http://www.adrc-tae.org/tiki-index.php?page=HomePage.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The ability to pay out of pocket for services must also be discussed with the family or other support persons. Although hospitals are not expected to have definitive knowledge of the terms of any given patient's insurance coverage or eligibility for community-based services,

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: or for Medicaid coverage, they are expected to have a general awareness of these matters and their impact on the patient's post-discharge needs and prospects for recovery. For example, if the patient is a Medicare beneficiary, the hospital is expected to be aware of Medicare coverage requirements for home health care or admission to a rehabilitation hospital, a skilled nursing facility, or a long term care hospital, etc. and to make the beneficiary aware that they may have to pay out of pocket for services not meeting the coverage requirements.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Similarly, for Medicaid, they should know coverage options for home health, attendant care, and long term care services or have contacts at the State Medicaid agency that can assist with these issues. As noted above, hospitals are also expected to have knowledge of community resources to assist in arranging services. Some examples include Aging and Disability Resource Centers and Centers for Independent Living (see box above).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For Information- Not Required/Not to be Cited

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Providing a discharge planning tool to patients and their family or other support persons may help to reinforce the discharge plan. Use of the tools may encourage patients' participation in developing the plan as well as provide them an easy-to-follow guide to prepare them for a successful transition from the hospital. The tool should be given to patients on admission, reviewed throughout their stay, and updated prior to discharge.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Examples of available tools include:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Medicare's "Your Discharge Planning Checklist," (available at http://www.medicare.gov/publications/pubs/pdf/11376.pdf)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Agency for Healthcare, Research and Quality's (AHRQ) "Taking Care of Myself: A Guide For When I Leave the Hospital," (available at http://www.ahrq.gov/qual/goinghomeguide.pdf)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Consumers Advancing Patient Safety (CAPS) "Taking Charge of Your Healthcare: Your Path to Being an Empowered Patient Toolkit" (available at http://www.patientsafety.org/page/transtoolkit/).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital CoP governing patients' rights at §482.13(b) provides that "The patient has the right to participate in the development and implementation of his or her plan of care." (CMS views discharge planning as part of the patient's plan of care). "The patient or his/her representative (as allowed under State law) has the right to make informed decisions regarding his/her care" and "The patient's rights include ... being involved in care planning and treatment." Accordingly, hospitals are expected to engage the patient, or the patient's representative, actively in the development of the discharge evaluation, not only as a source of information required for the assessment of self-care capabilities, but also to incorporate the patient's goals and preferences as much as possible into the evaluation. A patient's goals and preferences may be, in the hospital's view, unrealistic. Identifying divergent hospital and patient assessments of what is realistic enables a discussion of these differences and may result in an assessment and subsequent development of a discharge plan that has a better chance of successful implementation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: erences and may result in an assessment and subsequent development of a discharge plan that has a better chance of successful implementation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: For Information - Not Required/Not to be Cited

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If a patient exercises the right to refuse to participate in the discharge planning evaluation, documentation of the refusal is recommended in the medical record.

content: · In every unit with inpatient beds surveyed, is there evidence of discharge planning evaluation activities?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The patient's post-discharge care needs being met in the environment from which he/she entered the hospital? What the patient's care needs will be immediately upon discharge, and whether those needs are expected to remain constant or lessen over time?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The patient's insurance coverage (if applicable) and how that coverage might or might not provide for necessary services post-hospitalization?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · For patients admitted from home --

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Whether the patient can perform activities of daily living (personal hygiene and grooming, dressing and undressing, feeding, voluntary control over bowel and bladder, ambulation, etc.)?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · The patient's or family/other support person's ability to provide self- care/care?

content: · Whether the patient will require specialized medical equipment or home modification?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If yes, did the evaluation include an assessment of whether the equipment is available or if the modifications can be made to safely discharge the patient to that setting?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · If the patient or family/support person is unable to meet care needs or there are additional care needs above their capabilities, did the evaluation include an assessment of available community-based services to meet post-hospital needs?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · For patients admitted from a nursing facility, skilled nursing facility or assisted living facility did the evaluation assess whether the prior facility has the capability to provide necessary post-hospital services to the patient (i.e. is the same, higher, or lower level of care required and can those needs be met?)If yes, is there any documentation that the patient's care needs fall within the capabilities of the facility?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Are the results of the discharge planning evaluation documented in the medical record?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.43(b)(5) - The hospital personnel must complete the evaluation on a timely basis so that appropriate arrangements for post-hospital care are made before discharge, and to avoid unnecessary delays in discharge.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.43(b)(5)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: After a patient has been identified as needing an evaluation, or after a request for an evaluation has been made by the physician, patient and/or patient's representative, the evaluation must be completed timely. This means there must be sufficient time after completion to allow arrangements for post-hospital care to be made, without having to delay the patient's discharge in order to do so, or requiring the patient to transfer to a different setting from where he/she was admitted from primarily due to the delay in making appropriate arrangements. The comparatively short average length of stay of a short term acute care hospital inpatient necessitates prompt attention to patients' discharge planning needs in that type of hospital. Failure to complete the evaluation in a timely manner could make it more difficult to implement the patient's final discharge plan, and/or may cause an unnecessary delay in the patient's discharge from the hospital. While other types of hospitals with a longer average length of stay may be able to complete the evaluation at a later point after admission, they too must complete it on a timely basis to avoid delays in discharge.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: r average length of stay may be able to complete the evaluation at a later point after admission, they too must complete it on a timely basis to avoid delays in discharge.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Where a team approach is utilized by the hospital in developing the discharge planning evaluation, there must be a process to promote efficient collaboration among team members to complete the evaluation in a timely manner. Changes in patient condition throughout the hospitalization warrant adjustments to the discharge plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)

content: · Review a sample of cases to determine if the discharge planning evaluation was completed on a timely basis to allow for appropriate arrangements to be made for post- hospital care and to avoid delays in discharge. In order to assess this:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Determine when the discharge planning evaluation was initiated. If the evaluation was not begun within 24 hours of the request or identification of the need for an evaluation, ask why.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: · Is there a pattern of delayed start or completion of the evaluation? If so, is the delay due to circumstances beyond the hospital's control (e.g., inability to reach the beneficiary's support person(s), continuing changes in the patient's condition) and/or is the delay due to the hospital's failure to develop timely discharge planning evaluations?
