title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.61(c)(1)(ii) Short-term and long range goals;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.61(c)(1)(ii)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Based on the problems identified for treatment, short-term and long-range goals are developed. Whether the use of short-term or a combination of short-term and long-range goals is appropriate is dependent on the length of hospital stay.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Short-term and long-range goals include specific dates for expected achievement. As goals are achieved, the treatment plan should be revised. When a goal is modified, changed or discontinued without achievement, the plan should be reviewed for relevancy, and updated as needed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: In crisis intervention and short-term treatment there may be only one timeframe for treatment goals. As the length of hospital stay increases (often because of the long-term chronic nature of the patient's illness), both long-range and short-term goals are needed.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The long-range goal is achieved through the development of a series of short-term goals, i.e., smaller, logical sequential steps which will result in reaching the long-range goal. Both the short-term and long-range goals must be stated as expected behavioral outcomes for the patient. Goals must be related to the problems identified for treatment. Goals must be written as observable, measurable patient behaviors to be achieved. Discharge criteria may be included as long-range goals.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.61(c)(1)(ii)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: How do treatment plan goals relate to the problems being treated?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Do goals indicate the outcomes to be achieved by the patient?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are the goals written in a way that allow changes in the patient's behavior to be measured?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If not apparent, what criteria do staff use to measure success?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: How relevant are the treatment plan goals to the patient's condition?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-1643 (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.61(c)(1)(iii) The specific treatment modalities utilized;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.61(c)(1)(iii)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: This requirement refers to all of the planned treatment modalities used to treat the patient during hospitalization. Having identified the problems requiring treatment, and defining outcome goals to be achieved, appropriate treatment approaches must be identified.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Modalities include all of the active treatment measures provided to the patient. It describes the treatment that will be provided to the patient. It describes the treatment that will be provided by various staff.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A daily schedule of unit activities does not, in itself, constitute planned modalities of treatment. It is expected that when a patient attends various treatment modalities/activities, it is a part of individualized planning with a specific purpose and focus for that patient.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Simply "naming" modalities (i.e., individual therapy, group therapy, occupational therapy, medication education) is not acceptable. The focus of the treatment must be included.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Simply "stating" modality approaches (i.e., "set limits," "encourage socialization," "discharge planning as needed") is not acceptable. Modality approaches must be specifically described in order to assure consistency of approach.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Observation of staff implementing treatment, both in structured and non-structured settings, is a major criterion to determine whether active treatment is being provided in accordance with planned treatment.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: It must be clear to you that the active treatment received by the patient is internally consistent and not simply a series of disconnected specific modalities delivered within certain scheduled intervals.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.61(c)(1)(iii)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are qualified staff observed following the methods, approaches and staff intervention as stated?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Can staff explain the focus of the modality they have provided?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are observed treatment methods, approaches and interventions from all disciplines included in the plan?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Do the pieces of the treatment plan work together to achieve the greatest possible gain for the patient?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Does the hospital integrate its activities, therapies, treatments, and patient routines to work for the patient's therapeutic interest first, and its own convenience second?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Do the disciplines present at observed treatment planning meetings represent all of the patient's needs?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If the patient attends treatment planning, how do the staff prepare the patient to participate?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If the patient does not attend, what reasons do staff give to explain the absence? Is there a process to enable staff to reach a consensus regarding how treatment will be carried out?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Is the patient included in the decision-making, whenever possible?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are the final decisions regarding treatment approaches defined clearly by the end of the discussion?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: How does the patient get to know his/her treatment regime?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: How does the treatment team encourage the patient to accept responsibility for engaging in the treatment regime, rather than accepting it passively?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-1644 (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.61(c)(1)(iv) The responsibilities of each member of the treatment team; and Interpretive Guidelines §482.61(c)(1)(iv)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: There are no "correct" number of staff who comprise the treatment team. The disciplines involved in the patient's treatment depend upon the problems to be treated, the short-term and long-range goals and the treatment approaches and modalities used to achieve the goals.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The intent of the regulation is to insure that each individual on the treatment team who is primarily responsible for ensuring compliance with particular aspects of the patient's individualized treatment program is identified. Identification of the staff should be recorded in a manner that includes the name and discipline of the individual. If other professionals or paraprofessionals provide care, the facility has the latitude to decide the manner with which it will identify them on the treatment plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The patient, as well as family/significant others, should be aware of the staff responsible for various aspects of treatment.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.61(c)(1)(iv)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are staff who are designated in the treatment plan observed carrying out treatment activities and therapies? Is the information in the plan consistent with surveyor observations?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are the patients able to name the staff responsible for implementing their treatment? Is this information consistent with the treatment plan?

content: When the progress and treatment notes are reviewed, the content of the notes must relate to the treatment plan. The notes must indicate what the hospital staff is doing to carry out the treatment plan and the patient's response to the interventions.

content: §482.61(c)(2) The treatment received by the patient must be documented in such a way to assure that all active therapeutic efforts are included.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Active treatment is an essential requirement for inpatient psychiatric care. Active treatment is a clinical process involving ongoing assessment, diagnosis, intervention, evaluation of care and treatment, and planning for discharge and aftercare, under the direction of a psychiatrist. The patient is in the hospital because it has been determined that the patient requires intensive, 24 hour, specialized psychiatric intervention that cannot be provided outside the psychiatric hospital. The medical record must indicate that

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: the hospital adheres to the patient's right to be counseled about medication, its intended effects, and the potential side effects. If the patient requires, because of danger to self or others, a more restrictive environment, the hospital must indicate that the staff attempted to care for the patient in the least restrictive setting before progressing to a more restrictive setting.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Through observation, look for evidence that each patient is receiving all the aspects of treatment to which the hospital has committed itself based upon his/her assessment, evaluation and plan of care. It is the hospital's responsibility to provide those treatment modalities with sufficient frequency and intensity to assure that the patient achieves his/her optimal level of functioning.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Through observation and interviews, look for evidence that each patient's rights are being addressed and protected. There should be policies and procedures in place to address the following areas: informed consent, confidentiality, privacy, and security. Expect to see detailed policies and procedures regarding the therapeutic use of restrictions, such as visitors, mail, and phone calls. Seclusion and restraint policies and procedures must address patient protection and safety while in a restricted setting.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Clarification of the types of notes found in the medical record.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Treatment notes are recordings in the medical record that indicate provision of, and a patient's response to, a specific modality. This modality may be drug therapy, individual, family, marital, or group therapy, art therapy, recreational therapy, and any specialized therapy ordered by the physician or anyone credentialed by the facility, in accordance with the State law, to write orders in the medical record.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A combined treatment and progress note may be written.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Progress notes are recordings in the medical record that are written by persons directly responsible for the care and active treatment of the patient. Progress notes give a chronological picture of how the patient is progressing toward the accomplishment of the individual goals in the treatment plan. These are frequently shift notes, weekly notes, or monthly notes.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Refer to §482.61(c)(2) Interpretive Guidelines for clarification between treatment notes and progress notes. The recording of progress is evidence of individual patient performance. Specifically, the progress notes recorded by the professional staff, or others responsible for the patient's treatment, must give a chronological picture of the patient's progress or lack of progress towards attaining short and long-range goals outlined in the individual treatment plan. Progress notes should relate to the goals of the treatment plan. Notes that state, "patient slept well" or "no complaints" constitute observations and do not indicate how the patient is responding to treatment and progressing towards set goals. Frequency alone does not determine the adequacy of progress notes. Expect to see greater frequency when patients are more acutely ill and/or in a crisis of some kind. Notes should be dated and signed (signature and title or discipline).

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62 Condition of Participation: Special Staff Requirements for Psychiatric Hospitals

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must have adequate numbers of qualified professional and supportive staff to evaluate patients, formulate written, individualized comprehensive treatment plans, provide active treatment measures and engage in discharge planning.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The purpose of this Condition of Participation is to ensure that the psychiatric hospital is adequately staffed with qualified mental health professionals and supportive staff to carry out an intensive and comprehensive active treatment program and to protect and promote the physical and mental health of the patients.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Through observation, interview and record review determine if numbers and/or deployment of qualified staff is a concern. Review incident reports, medication error reports, patient and staff injury reports, for indications that staffing is an issue.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Adequate numbers are defined to mean the numbers, and deployment, of staff with qualifications to evaluate, plan, implement and document active treatment.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Do not look at numbers alone. The hospital is responsible for organizing its available staff and administrative duties along with patient appointments, treatment plan meetings, treatment sessions, activities, materials, equipment and patient assignments to wards and groups in such a way that results in patients achieving the maximum therapeutic benefit.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedure §482.62

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Assess the adequacy of the Special Staffing Condition by:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 1. Observing sampled patients and others during structured sessions and in unstructured settings. You should be able to observe behavioral evidence of a rational organization of resources.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 2. Next, interview patients and staff to determine whether or not necessary treatment modalities and other services are being provided in a timely manner.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 3. Next review the medical records of patients in the sample to ascertain if necessary active treatment assessments, treatments, evaluations and activities have been conducted and documented.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 4. Also, review other records such as restraint and seclusion records, incident reports, medication error reports, reports of patient/staff injuries, etc., to determine the extent to which staffing levels or deployment contributed to negative patient outcomes.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 5. Evaluate all outcome data in light of the success or failure observed during the survey relevant to each patient receiving active treatment, and achieving desired outcomes of care. This is the primary basis for evaluating the adequacy of the hospital's staffing under this Special Condition.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Active treatment occurs when the patient receives treatment interventions that are delivered under the direction of a physician, and which are specific to patient strengths,

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: disabilities, and problems identified in the treatment plan. Treatment interventions and other services are furnished in accordance with accepted standards of professional practice. Although the active treatment process must be identifiable in documentation, it must be first and foremost observable and evident in daily practice.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Treatment interventions need to be individualized, in that the patient receives assistance with resolving or ameliorating the problems/circumstances that led to hospitalization. Expect to see treatment focused on the unique needs of individual patients. For example, several patients may be referred to "Anger Management Group," but the focus of discussion and therapeutic intervention may differ depending on the individual patient's particular issue regarding managing anger.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Whether structure must be imposed by staff or whether the patient can direct his or her own activities for periods of time (without staff supervision), is based on the patient's ability to engage in constructive, appropriate behavior (without engaging in harm to self or others). Be certain that the patient's time on the unit is maximized toward the further development of appropriate desired outcomes, including but not limited to leisure and recreation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(b) Standard: Director of inpatient psychiatric services; medical staff. Inpatient psychiatric services must be under the supervision of a clinical director, service chief, or equivalent who is qualified to provide the leadership required for an intensive treatment program ...

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(b)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Inpatient psychiatric services include the following functions: admission interviews, assessments and evaluations; psychiatric and medical work-ups; treatment team leadership; medication management; on-call provision of emergency psychiatric and medical treatment; provision of individual, group and family therapies; provision of clinical supervision to other professionals and paraprofessionals; provision of medical and psychiatric educational workshops and conferences for all staff; and provision of consultation to staff for clinical and/or administrative matters.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The clinical director is ultimately responsible for the medical and psychiatric care that is provided to patients. The clinical director should ascertain that quality improvement programs are in place to monitor all areas of patient care, and should implement educational programs for all levels of staff.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedure §482.62(b)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Just prior to the end of the survey, schedule a meeting with the clinical director. By the time of this meeting, you should already have conducted required observation, interviews and record reviews for at least a majority of the patients in the sample. Collect any additional information that is necessary to consider in light of outcomes observed for patients, including: the qualifications of the clinical director; the leadership exhibited for the scope of psychiatric/medical treatment programs needed by patients; and the rationale for medical staffing coverage. If necessary, follow-up on letters of complaint previously reported serious problems, discrepancies with Data Collection Medical Staff Coverage (CMS-729).

content: The number of full-time, part-time and consulting staff, who are board certified within each category and their availability to the hospital must be adequate to provide psychiatric services, as described above. Adequacy is considered in light of the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: How are medical staff deployed? To what programs/units are they assigned? Why?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: How much time do physicians spend on the units? Based on observations, interviews, and medical record reviews is coverage adequate to meet the needs of sampled patients? To meet the needs of other patients observed during the survey?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(b)(1) The clinical director, service chief or equivalent must meet the training and experience requirements for examination by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology, or the American Osteopathic Board of Neurology and Psychiatry.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(b)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A physician is qualified to take the examinations for board certification upon successful completion of a psychiatric residency program approved by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology and/or the American Osteopathic Board of Psychiatry and Neurology.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.62(b)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Review the clinical director's personnel folder or ask the clinical director if he/she has one of the following:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: a. Certification of the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology and/or certification of the American Osteopathic Board of Neurology and Psychiatry.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: b. If no certification, evidence that the person took the Boards would satisfy that the person had the training and equivalency to be admitted to the board examination.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: c. If indicated, medical school and residency training

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: d. Length of time he has been employed at the facility; length of time he has been at his position

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: To be admitted to the American Board Examinations the following conditions must be met:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 1. License without restrictions

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 2. Graduation from a medical school approved by either the Medical Osteopathic Association or the American Medical Association.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 3. A successful completion of an approved residency-training program for at least 3 years before 1988 that the America Council on Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) approves. After 1988, it has to be a four year accredited program.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(b)(2) The director must monitor and evaluate the quality and appropriateness of services and treatment provided by the medical staff.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(b)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Services and treatment prescribed to patients must be in accordance with appropriate and acceptable standards of practice.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: In states that allow psychologists to have admitting privileges, it is still the responsibility of the clinical director to oversee the quality of the patient's treatment.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.62 (b)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: What mechanisms does the director use to monitor and evaluate the work of the medical staff (personal interviews? Quality Improvement reports? incident reports?)?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: When problems are discovered by the clinical director, how are they corrected?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are services, notes, and reports timely?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are medications used appropriately for the patient's diagnosis?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-1695 (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(c) Standard: Availability of medical personnel.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Doctors of medicine or osteopathy and other appropriate professional personnel must be available to provide necessary medical and surgical diagnostic and treatment services. If medical and surgical diagnostic services and treatment are not available within the institution, the institution must have an agreement with an outside source of these services to ensure that they are immediately available or a satisfactory agreement must be established for transferring patients to a general hospital that participates in the Medicare program.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(c)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Contracts or other arrangements with individuals and/or providers assure that medical and surgical services are available to meet the needs of the patients. Review the medical and surgical services provided by the hospital during the interview with the clinical director.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Discuss contract or arrangements with the clinical director for services provided off grounds.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.62(c)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: How did the hospital meet the medical/surgical/diagnostic needs represented by each patient in the sample? Were these done timely? Appropriately?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If contracts are not current or available, how are these services provided for the patient, if needed? Is there evidence of negative outcomes as a result of these arrangements?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are reports from other services such as pharmacy, radiology, and clinical laboratory timely? Appropriate?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-1700 (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(d) Standard: Nursing services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital or unit must have a qualified director of psychiatric nursing services. In addition to the director of nursing, there must be adequate numbers of registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, and mental health workers to provide nursing care necessary under each patient's active treatment program and to maintain progress notes on each patient.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(d)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Psychiatric nursing functions may include the following: supervision of paraprofessional staff; assessment, planning, provision, and evaluation of psychiatric nursing care to patients; medication teaching; management of the therapeutic milieu; provision of mandatory and voluntary in-service training to all staff; and provision of specialized treatments and therapies, such as individual, group and family therapies, that require the clinical expertise of a professional psychiatric nurse.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Expect to see evidence of orientation programs as well as ongoing continuing education programs for Licensed Practical Nurses and mental health workers that stress individualized treatment interventions.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Determine that there is a qualified Director of Nursing (DON) providing the required leadership and supervision for the psychiatric nursing department.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(d)(1) The director of psychiatric nursing services must be a registered nurse who has a master's degree in psychiatric or mental health nursing or its equivalent from a school of nursing accredited by the National League for Nursing, or be qualified by education and experience in the care of the mentally ill . . .

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(d)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: During the interview with the DON, assess his/her educational background and psychiatric nursing and leadership skills. If the DON has less than a Master's Degree in Psychiatric Nursing, expect to see evidence of experience and on-going training in psychiatric nursing. Documented consultation from a nurse with a Master's in Psychiatric Nursing constitutes on-going training.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.62(d)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are nursing assessments completed on all patients?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Do the multidisciplinary treatment plans reflect nursing input which include specific nursing interventions for nursing problems (e.g. violence toward self/others, physical/medical crises)?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Is nursing care evaluated by an R.N., with changes in the care based on the patient's progress or lack thereof?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are intrusive techniques (e.g. seclusion, restraint, electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), and/or medical procedures) and patient incidents (e.g. medication errors, patient falls, patient-to-patient and patient-to-staff injuries) monitored in accordance with hospital policy, State statutes and safe nursing practice?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are nursing personnel observed relating to patients in a therapeutic manner?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(d)(1) ... The director must demonstrate competence to participate in interdisciplinary formulation of individual treatment plans; to give skilled nursing care and therapy; and to direct, monitor, and evaluate the nursing care furnished.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(d)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Based on structured observations of the patients in the sample and other patients in the hospital, patient and staff interviews and medical record review, ascertain that nursing services are provided in accordance with safe, acceptable standards of nursing practice.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Information obtained from the DON should include: implementation of continuous quality improvement programs; provision of orientation, in-service and continuing education programs for nursing personnel especially in the areas of psychiatric nursing, nursing process, prevention and management of violence, CPR and Universal Precautions.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-1703 (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(d)(2) The staffing pattern must ensure the availability of a registered nurse 24 hours each day. ...

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(d)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Guidance is pending and will be updated in future release

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(d)(2) ... There must be adequate numbers of registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, and mental health workers to provide the nursing care necessary under each patient's active treatment program.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(d)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The evaluation of sufficient numbers and level of RNs, LPNs and mental health workers is based on the patient characteristics as seen in structured observations of patients in the sample and other patients in the hospital, patient interviews, and as evidenced in medical records and other data related to patients (e.g. incident reports, seclusion/restraint reports). Patient care assignments should be appropriate to the skills and qualifications of the nursing personnel providing patient care.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: There should be evidence that all nursing personnel have education, experience and/or training in psychiatric care. Mental health workers spend the majority of their workday interacting with patients. Expect to see evidence that they are receiving on-going supervision and training. Mental health workers should be assigned patient care duties and therapeutic modalities that reflect their educational level, psychiatric training, and experience.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedure §482.62(d)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The nursing staffing patterns should be reviewed on a sample of approximately 25% of the certified wards. The staffing, including levels of nursing personnel, should be reviewed for the day(s) of the survey and evaluated based on the level of needs presented by the patients. Additional staffing patterns shall be reviewed if a problem or concern is evidenced. Decisions regarding extent of additional data (number of wards and dates) to be reviewed shall be based on the degree of problem/concern. Patient need assessment/patient acuity shall be reviewed for any wards as deemed necessary based on problems/concerns found in the sampling review.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If your observations and/or interviews indicate a staffing problem, you may want to consider the following variables in assessing adequacy of nursing personnel coverage:

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 1. Organization and types of services provided to patients by the nursing department;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 2. Number and levels of nursing care needs of patients, including average length of stay, acuity of patients and nursing care requirements;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 3. Number and levels of nursing personnel based on the roles and functions required of nursing;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 4. Number of suicidal/assaultive patients;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 5. Seclusion/restraint incidents;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 6. Number of admissions and discharges;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 7. Number and type of accidents and/or injuries;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 8. Amount and complexity of medication regimens;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 9. Medication errors;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 10. Use of P.R.N. (as needed) medications;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 11. Medical (physical) procedures;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 12. Assignment and utilization of "pool" nursing personnel (those staff who are hired through a contract service and are not employees of the hospital). Contractual staff should receive orientation and training necessary for assigned functions, and should be supervised by employees of the hospital;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 13. Availability of RNs to supervise/consult with nursing/non-nursing personnel about patient care;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 14. Availability of RNs to assess and implement care in crisis situations;

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 15. Availability of RNs to interact with patients in structured activities; and

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: 16. Involvement of patients with personnel.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(e) Standard: Psychological Services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must provide or have available psychological services to meet the needs of the patients.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(e)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Psychology services may include the following: diagnostic testing and diagnostic formulations on request from physicians; provision of individual, group and family therapies; participation in multi-disciplinary treatment conferences; and program development and evaluation.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The number of full-time, part-time and consulting psychologists must be adequate to provide necessary services to patients. Arrangements with outside resources must assure that necessary patient services will be provided.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.62(e)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Did the patients in the sample have a need for psychological services or testing? Were they provided in a timely manner and with sufficient intensity?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Did any of the patients in the sample indicate a need for psychological services, but none were requested?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: What types of psychological services are offered? (e.g., assessments, therapy)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Do certain groups of patients receive testing routinely? Dementia?, Children?, Adolescents? Why?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Once tests are performed, are results reported in sufficient time to be integrated in the patient's active treatment and treatment plan?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: How does the hospital or Psychological Service Department determine whether or not: it meets the needs of patients? Its services are underutilized or over-utilized?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Why have psychological services staff been deployed in the manner that they have?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-1715 (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(f) Standard: Social Services.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: There must be a director of social services who monitors and evaluates the quality and appropriateness of social services furnished. The services must be furnished in accordance with accepted standards of practice and established policies and procedures.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(f)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Social work functions may include the following functions: Intake or admission screening, psychosocial assessment of a newly admitted patient; developing an update or detailed re-assessment of the patient; high-social risk case finding; contact with family and others significant in the patient's life. Such functions may include patient and family

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: education, support, and advocacy; providing coordination/liaison with community-based social and mental health agency(ies) regarding the pre-admission status of the patient; participating as a member of the treatment team in development of treatment planning and subsequent planned interventions (modalities). Such modalities may include supportive, individual, couple, family, or group therapy, aimed at meeting specified goals identified in the treatment plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Continuity of care is an important social work principle and may be demonstrated through case management and a major role in discharge planning. Activities, in conjunction with the patient wishes, may include contact with patient's family, identifying and assisting in referral of the patient to community-based agency(ies) at the time of discharge. Finally, post-discharge follow-up may be done to assure that linkage of the patient with community resources has occurred to reduce re-hospitalization.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Determine who completed the assessment required by §482.61(a)(4) and initiated preliminary discharge planning. When staff other than a Social Worker perform these duties, the Director of Social Work or a Master's level social worker (MSW) qualified supervisory staff member should be involved to oversee the quality and appropriateness of service provided.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Patient and staff interviews, structured observations and review of selected medical records yield the information necessary to determine how well social work has met the needs of the patients. The surveyor should evaluate these data to determine adequacy of qualified and support staff deployed to patient areas and their duties.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The social work policies for service provision to the patient should describe: the organizational structure of the department (program) and the range of services performed by the department.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedure §482.62(f)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Just prior to the end of the survey, schedule a meeting with the Director of Social Work. By the time of the meeting, you should already have conducted required observations, interviews and record reviews for at least a majority of the patients in the sample. Collect any additional information that is necessary to consider in light of outcomes observed for patients, including: the qualifications of the director; the leadership exhibited for the scope of services needed by the patient; and the rationale for social work staffing coverage.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: How does the director periodically audit the quality of social work services furnished?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: What are the outcomes of audits conducted? What percentage of psychosocial assessments was completed and available in written form at the time of the interdisciplinary treatment plan? How does the patient's social needs as addressed by the social worker in the psychosocial assessment compare against the goals developed in the interdisciplinary treatment plan?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Has social work staff provided active treatment in accordance with the patient's treatment plan?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Accepted standards of practice are based on policy statements adopted by the National Association of Social Workers and a definition of social work practice in health care adapted by the Consortium of Health Care Social Work Organizations. Staff should adhere to the facility's personnel requirements.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(f)(1) The director of the social work department or service must have a master's degree from an accredited school of social work or must be qualified by education and experience in the social services needs of the mentally ill. If the director does not hold a master's degree in social work, at least one staff member must have this qualification.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(f)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The duties, functions, and responsibilities of the director of social services/social work should be clearly delineated and documented in the facility's policies and procedures. If the director is not MSW qualified and at least one staff member is MSW qualified, verify the duties, functions, and responsibilities of the MSW.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.62(f)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: What are the director's qualifications, experience and scope of duties within this position?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: If a MSW staff member, other than the director, is performing any of these duties, what are this staff member's experience and scope of duties performed? Why were these duties delegated?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: To what extent is the director's knowledge of the social work needs of the various wards? Why has the social work staff and services provided throughout the hospital been deployed in the manner it has?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(f)(2) Social service staff responsibilities must include, but are not limited to, participating in discharge, planning, arranging for follow-up care, and developing mechanisms for exchange of appropriate information with sources outside the hospital.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(f)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Social work contact with the patient, family, and significant others should occur during, or as soon as possible, after the admission. High-risk case finding should result in significant data being available for early integration into the treatment plan and subsequent social work action as indicated. The treatment team should consider, for possible inclusion into the patient's treatment plan, the anticipated social work role and expected interventions as recommended in the psychosocial assessment . Treatment and discharge planning activities, liaison/follow-up efforts should be based upon the goals, including discharge goals, and staff responsibilities specified in the treatment plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.62(f)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are social work staff routinely involved in providing services to the patient that are identified in the treatment plan?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: To what extent do social work staff provide discharge planning services to the patient in the way of: supportive individual, couple, family, or group therapy focused on discharge goals of the patient? Carrying out a liaison role with community resource providers?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Have social work staff assured that adequate information is provided to post-hospital patient service providers?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-1720 (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(g) Standard: Therapeutic Activities.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital must provide a therapeutic activities program.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(g)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A variety of therapeutic and rehabilitative activities are selectively used as therapeutic tools in providing active treatment to the psychiatric patients. Therapeutic activities focus upon the development and maintenance of adaptive skills that will improve the patient's functioning. In contrast, leisure activities provide the patient with individualized opportunities to acquire knowledge, skills and attitudes about meaningful leisure involvement and experiences. A patient may need treatment and/or remediation of functional behavior(s) prior to leisure involvement. However, for some psychiatric patients the priority need may be for leisure education and activities.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-1725 (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(g)(1) The program must be appropriate to the needs and interests of patients and be directed toward restoring and maintaining optimal levels of physical and psychosocial functioning.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(g)(1)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The hospital is responsible for ensuring consistent availability and provision of individualized therapeutic activities and rehabilitative services based on patient needs.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: The selection of individualized therapeutic and rehabilitative staff modalities should be based on patient need and goals set in the patient's treatment plan. Rehabilitative services may include educational, occupational, recreational, physical, art, dance, music, and speech therapies and vocational rehabilitation evaluation and counseling. There are other disciplines that also serve patients. Consultants include but are not limited to the following: educational instructors, registered occupational therapist/certified occupational therapy assistant, certified therapeutic recreation specialist, certified therapeutic recreation assistant, speech-language pathologist has certificate of clinical competence, registered and certified music therapist, registered art therapist, and registered physical therapist. The qualified vocational specialist may perform duties of a rehabilitation counselor, vocational evaluator, or the work adjustment specialist.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: A-1726 (Rev. 200, Issued: 02-21-20; Effective: 02-21-20, Implementation: 02-21-20)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: §482.62(g)(2) The number of qualified therapists, support personnel, and consultants must be adequate to provide comprehensive therapeutic activities consistent with each patient's active treatment program.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Interpretive Guidelines §482.62(g)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Qualified staff should complete their respective discipline assessments for use in multidisciplinary treatment planning. Specific role(s) and modalities to be implemented by rehabilitative staff must be determined by goals set in the patient's treatment plan.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Qualified therapists who provide clinical services and administrative staff should utilize established monitoring and evaluation mechanisms to conduct consistent timely review of the quality and appropriateness of therapeutic and rehabilitative services delivered to patients.

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Survey Procedures §482.62(g)(2)

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Is there evidence that sampled patients and staff are familiar with the goals and staff interventions described in the patient's treatment plan? Are these observed interventions being carried out? What is the patient's response? Are these interventions and activities of sufficient frequency and intensity to achieve maximum therapeutic benefit?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: What are the qualifications, experience, duties and responsibilities of the Therapeutic Activities Director and discipline supervisor(s)?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: How is the program organized?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Did the patients in the sample have a need for any therapeutic activities? Were their needs met?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Did any of the patients in the sample indicate a need for therapeutic activities, but none were considered?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: What kinds of services are provided to the patient population?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Are activity areas/sites accessible and available to meet the patient's individual needs? Are the facilities and resources adequate to enable implementation of goals set in the patient's treatment plan?

title: CMS State Operations Manual - Appendix A (Hospitals)
content: Does the program utilize available community resources to provide opportunities for socialization, leisure, and therapeutic and/or rehabilitation activities for patients who can participate outside the hospital setting?
